aliases: ephemeral cache billing overhead per turn
cache write cost on trivial turns
signals.review_reason: Direct financial impact of ~$5K/month in unnecessary cache write costs. The cache_read mechanism works correctly but the SDK additionally re-writes ~65K tokens per turn, effectively paying 1.25x write rate for content already cached. This is a sustained, quantifiable cost loss affecting all long-lived SDK sessions.

source_issues.title: cache issues in sdk
source_issues.evidence: 65K-73K cache_creation_input_tokens per turn regardless of message size (even 'ok thanks'). cache_read accumulates correctly but cache_create adds ~65K fresh on top every turn. Per-turn cost $0.50-0.65 for trivial exchanges. Fleet-wide ~$175/day = ~$5K/month attributable to this floor. Byte-stable system prompts still trigger full 65K rewrite.

signals.topic: API 400 errors with empty body repeatedly block user conversations, with canRetry=false preventing automatic recovery
signals.summary: API returns 400 status with no response body (no body) on 8+ occasions over 1.5 hours, completely blocking agent workflow. canRetry=false prevents automatic retry, forcing manual restart. Error message lacks diagnostic detail for root cause identification.
signals.review_reason: Workflow-blocking errors that occur repeatedly within a single session. canRetry=false makes each occurrence a hard block requiring manual intervention. Lack of response body prevents root cause diagnosis (auth vs rate-limit vs format). Each incident fully blocks the user's agent task.

source_issues.title: 400 status code (no body)
source_issues.evidence: 8 occurrences of 400 status code with empty body over 1.5 hours on custom connection. canRetry=false makes all failures terminal. User workflow completely blocked with no diagnostic information (no response body to determine if auth/format/rate-limit issue). Errors reported at T+245s, T+903s, T+1349s, T+1754s.

signals.topic: outputFormat returns subtype='success' with undefined structured_output for non-trivial schemas, breaking downstream parsing
signals.summary: When using outputFormat with complex/nested JSON schemas, the SDK returns subtype='success' but structured_output is undefined. The correct JSON exists in raw result text but is not extracted. Any code relying on structured_output gets undefined with no error signal.
aliases: outputFormat extraction failure on nested schemas
json_schema outputFormat broken for complex schemas
structured output not returned despite success status
signals.review_reason: Users relying on structured_output from outputFormat receive undefined values with no error signal. Since subtype='success', error handling code cannot detect the failure. This causes silent data loss for any downstream consumer using structured_output. The feature is fundamentally broken for non-trivial schemas.

source_issues.title: outputFormat returns subtype 'success' when structured_output is absent
source_issues.evidence: Nested schemas (3+ levels) consistently return subtype='success' with structured_output=undefined. Simple 2-field schemas work correctly. The raw JSON is correct in result text but SDK fails to extract/validate it. Downstream consumers expecting structured_output get silent undefined. Multiple schema variations tested: nested without $ref, deep with $ref, inlined with additionalProperties:false — all fail the same way.

signals.topic: sandbox.network.allowedDomains configuration is silently ignored for Bash tool and WebFetch, breaking intended security boundary
signals.summary: The sandbox.network.allowedDomains option is accepted by the SDK but has zero enforcement on Bash subprocess network calls or WebFetch requests. All network access is unrestricted regardless of configuration. No OS-level enforcement (no proxy, no seccomp/bubblewrap).
aliases: Bash network access not blocked by sandbox config
signals.review_reason: Security boundary misconfiguration — SDK accepts domain restrictions but never enforces them. This creates a false security guarantee for users relying on sandbox.network.allowedDomains to restrict outbound network access. Unlike other bugs, this does not actively block user workflows but creates a significant security gap in deployments that depend on network isolation.

source_issues.title: sandbox.network.allowedDomains not enforced for Bash tool or WebFetch
source_issues.evidence: With sandbox.network.allowedDomains=['*.walmart.com'], curl to google.com via Bash tool succeeds. WebFetch to google.com also succeeds. SDK documentation claims domain restrictions apply but no enforcement mechanism exists. Users relying on this config for security isolation have a false sense of protection.

signals.topic: Action fails on PRs with newly added files — git hash-object called before PR checkout
signals.summary: The action calls git hash-object on changed files in PRs before checking out the PR branch, causing immediate failure for any PR that introduces new files. No workaround exists from workflow config; users must fall back to local CLI.
aliases: git hash-object failure for new files
signals.review_reason: This blocks the main PR review/use case for any PR that introduces new files — an extremely common real-world scenario. The action exits with code 1 before any Claude work begins. No configuration workaround exists, forcing users to abandon the GitHub Action entirely and use the CLI locally. This is a hard workflow blocker.

source_issues.title: Action fails on PRs with newly added files - git hash-object called before PR checkout
source_issues.evidence: Action exits with fatal: could not open '<file>' for reading: No such file or directory for every ADDED file. Stack trace points to fetcher.ts:354 in prepareTagMode before PR checkout. No workflow-level workaround available; users must fall back to local CLI.

signals.topic: GitHub App 'not installed' error breaks previously-working workflows across multiple repos
signals.summary: Previously-functional workflows across multiple repos began failing with 'Claude Code is not installed on this repository' errors after an unknown event. The only resolution required reinstalling the Claude GitHub App on the org, with no corresponding audit log events.
aliases: Claude Code is not installed error
signals.review_reason: Workflows broke completely across an entire GitHub organization with no actionable error message. Users had to discover and manually reinstall the GitHub App despite no visible uninstallation event. While only one org is in the evidence, the pattern of app auth silently breaking across all repos in an org is a significant reliability issue that users cannot debug without external investigation.

source_issues.title: [BUG] "Claude Code is not installed on this repository" for previously-working github actions across multiple repos on 2026-04-28
source_issues.evidence: Failing on every PR across multiple repos in the same organization with exit code 1. No audit log events for app uninstallation. Only fix: manually reinstall Claude App on the org. Correlated with connector addition in the same org around the same time.

signals.topic: Internal 'directory mismatch' error causes total workflow failure on every run
signals.summary: Every triggered run produces an 'Internal error: directory mismatch for .../claude-code-action/<ref>/tsconfig.json' error and exits with code 1. Switching refs does not resolve the issue. Users disabled the workflow entirely as a workaround.
signals.review_reason: The action fails completely on every invocation with exit code 1, producing an 'Internal error' that indicates a bug in the action itself. Users cannot run the action at all and had to completely disable the workflow. This is a hard workflow blocker for the affected users, even though only one repo is documented.

source_issues.title: Internal error: directory mismatch for ".../claude-code-action/<ref>/tsconfig.json", fd 4 — fails on every run
source_issues.evidence: 7 consecutive failures on the same repo with the same error before any tool dispatch. Exit code 1 every time. Switching between @v1 (floating tag) and SHA pin both fail identically. User disabled the workflow trigger as a workaround, routing all AI tasks to a local cursor-agent dispatch script.

signals.topic: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands (awk, python3 -c, Windows paths)
signals.summary: The safety detector incorrectly blocks legitimate bash commands containing && within awk patterns, python3 -c inline scripts, and file paths with '0:' suffixes, causing jobs to accumulate permission blocks until turns are exhausted and the job is cancelled.
signals.review_reason: Legitimate Claude commands are blocked, wasting the user's available turns and eventually cancelling the entire job. Users lose meaningful work and must manually work around the false positives. While count is 1, the evidence of job cancellation from turn exhaustion represents significant disruption to the main workflow.

source_issues.title: False positive multi-operation detection blocks valid bash commands (awk, python3 -c, Windows path pattern)
source_issues.evidence: Claude's own legitimate commands are blocked as multiple operations or suspicious Windows paths, accumulating to exhaustion of 80 turns before job cancellation with 'Error: The operation was canceled.' User had to resort to instructing Claude to avoid certain legitimate patterns entirely as a workaround.

signals.topic: Trigger phrase case-sensitive matching causes silent failure on mobile (iOS autocorrect)
signals.summary: The trigger phrase regex lacks the case-insensitive flag, so '@Claude' (auto-capitalized by iOS) is silently rejected even though GitHub's workflow guard passes it through. The action exits with no signal to the user.
signals.review_reason: Mobile users (iOS) cannot successfully invoke the bot because their platform auto-capitalizes the trigger phrase, which the action then silently ignores. The workflow runs (creating confusion), but the action does nothing. Users receive no feedback, making this a silent failure in a primary interaction flow.

source_issues.title: trigger_phrase matching is case-sensitive, should be case-insensitive
source_issues.evidence: On iOS, '@claude' is auto-capitalized to '@Claude'. GitHub's workflow-level contains() check passes (case-insensitive), so the workflow runs. But the action's internal regex rejects it silently, skipping all steps with no user-visible signal. Mobile users have no indication why the bot did not respond.

signals.topic: Claude Code Security Review 缺乏请求节流机制导致频繁触发 API 速率限制阻断工作流
signals.summary: 用户运行 Claude Code Security Review 时因缺乏请求节流功能，频繁触发组织的 10,000 tokens/min 速率限制，导致 API 返回 429 错误，工作流被阻断。用户明确要求添加节流/限速功能。
signals.review_reason: 虽然 count=1，但 reviewer 必须保留，原因如下：(1) 用户影响证据明确：API 429 错误直接阻断 Claude Code Security Review 的主流程，用户无法完成安全审查；(2) 需求明确：用户明确提出功能缺失——'there should be a way of throttling the requests'，说明产品层面缺少速率控制能力；(3) 属于 quota_rate_limit 类别中的主流程阻断场景，优先级应为 P1。count=1 不触发 P0 的'高频'条件，但明确阻断证据已足够支撑保留。

source_issues.title: I'm getting rate limited all the time
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告运行安全审查时持续触发 429 速率限制错误：'API Error: Request rejected (429) · This request would exceed your organization's rate limit of 10,000 input tokens per minute'，并明确要求'there should be a way of throttling the requests'。工作流被阻断，无替代方案。

signals.topic: MCP tool structuredContent drops human-readable content[].text, breaking model-visible tool output
signals.summary: When an MCP tool returns both content[].text and structuredContent, Claude Code CLI forwards only structuredContent to the model, silently dropping the text part. This breaks MCP App patterns that use text for human-presentable output (e.g., markdown-linked lists) while keeping structuredContent as typed payload. Works correctly on claude.ai web and ChatGPT.
signals.review_reason: Core MCP integration broken: tool results that include both human-readable text and structured data silently lose the text channel in Claude Code CLI. This blocks MCP App picker patterns and forces developers to duplicate human-readable content into structuredContent as a workaround. The user impact is confirmed with wire-side verification and cross-platform comparison showing it works on other hosts.

source_issues.title: MCP: tool result content[].text dropped from model when structuredContent is also present
source_issues.evidence: MCP tool returns both content[].text and structuredContent but only structuredContent reaches the model; user reports verified via wire-side logging and cross-platform comparison (works on claude.ai and ChatGPT, fails on Claude Code CLI). Model explicitly tells user it did not receive the text part.

signals.topic: Windows: Edit/Write permissions.allow rules in settings.json silently ignored
signals.summary: On Windows, the Edit and Write tool allow rules in ~/.claude/settings.json do not suppress permission prompts, even in bare form (no path). Bash allow rules in the same file work correctly, confirming the file is parsed. This forces manual approval for every file edit.
signals.review_reason: Core file-editing workflow blocked on Windows. Despite settings.json being parsed and Bash allow rules working from the same file, Edit and Write tool allow rules are silently ignored, causing permission prompts on every file operation. User must manually approve every edit — a direct, high-friction blocker for the primary use case.

source_issues.title: Edit and Write allow rules in ~/.claude/settings.json are ignored on Windows; Bash allow rules work
source_issues.evidence: Six tested forms of Edit/Write allow rules (Windows backslash, forward slash, POSIX paths, bare, tilde+symlink) all fire permission prompts after full restarts. Same settings file's Bash allow rules silence prompts correctly. User must manually approve every single file edit.

signals.topic: macOS auto-memory keyed to HOME-dir hash instead of cwd hash, mixing context across all projects
signals.summary: On macOS, Claude Code's auto-memory reads/writes from a path keyed only to the HOME directory hash regardless of the current working directory. Different project directories under the same HOME share one memory blob, making per-project memory effectively unusable.
signals.review_reason: Per-project memory context scoping is broken on macOS by design. All projects under the same HOME share a single memory blob, causing context pollution across unrelated domains. This makes auto-memory fundamentally unreliable for the primary target platform (macOS), directly defeating its documented purpose.

source_issues.title: [BUG] macOS auto-memory scoped to home-dir hash, ignoring cwd-hash dirs
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction confirmed across two CC versions on macOS. CC running at ~/utopia writes memory to ~/.claude/projects/-Users-leofloa/ instead of ~/.claude/projects/-Users-leofloa-utopia/. Linux build uses correct cwd-hash path matching the documentation. All macOS projects share one memory directory, mixing unrelated context.

signals.topic: Windows PowerShell permission classifier crashes on long settings, denying all PowerShell calls
signals.summary: On Windows, when additionalDirectories or other long settings fields accumulate enough entries, the PowerShell permission classifier subprocess crashes with 'command line too long'. This denies ALL PowerShell tool calls, including allowlisted commands, making the PowerShell allowlist effectively non-functional.
aliases: PowerShell permission classifier command line too long
signals.review_reason: Core Windows PowerShell workflow is blocked. The permission classifier crashes when settings fields are reasonably populated, silently denying ALL PowerShell tool calls including explicitly allowlisted safe commands. Users must audit and drastically reduce their additionalDirectories entries to restore functionality.

source_issues.title: Windows: PowerShell permission classifier fails 'command line too long' when additionalDirectories list is large
source_issues.evidence: Reproduced across 6 probes on a real Windows install with 38 additionalDirectories entries. Every PowerShell call returns 'permission denials: pwsh exited with code 1: The command line is too long' including trivially safe allowlisted commands like Get-ChildItem. Pruning to 4 entries restores expected behavior.

signals.topic: Voice dictation Trigger: pausing mid-dictation or stopping before Enter clears all transcribed text
signals.summary: On Linux (Ubuntu), pausing mid-dictation or stopping before pressing Enter clears all previously transcribed text. This is a regression — the feature worked in a prior version.
signals.review_reason: Voice dictation is a primary input method. The regression causes all transcribed text to be lost when the user pauses or stops before confirming with Enter, making the feature unreliable for its intended use case. User confirms this is a regression from a working prior version.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Trigger: pausing mid-dictation or stopping before pressing Enter clears all transcribed text
source_issues.evidence: User-reported regression on Ubuntu 24.04 with Logitech MX Brio USB mic. Pausing mid-dictation or stopping before pressing Enter causes all transcribed text to be lost. Prior version worked correctly. Confirmed as regression by user.

signals.topic: Streaming assistants misread out-of-context user messages as answers due to async tool latency
signals.summary: When streaming assistants perform slow async tool calls (e.g., 8s), users may send unrelated messages ('brb', 'I'll be on Telegram') during the wait. The assistant then reads the latest user message upon finishing and misinterprets it as the answer to its own follow-up question, causing wrong downstream actions.
aliases: mid-tool user message treated as answer
signals.review_reason: Describes a structural runtime bug causing wrong assistant actions: slow async tool calls create a race condition where user context messages are misread as answers. This is a real workflow error with a concrete reference implementation — it matches the '反复失败' (repeated failure) dimension of the pain point definition.

source_issues.title: Pattern: timestamp-aware context check for streaming assistants
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly describes a structural bug where streaming assistants that do slow work between turns can receive out-of-context messages they have no way to distinguish from real answers, causing the assistant to act on wrong inputs.

signals.topic: Skills introduction notebook omits GitHub repo clone as prerequisite, blocking first-time users
signals.summary: The skills introduction notebook on platform.claude.com tells users to 'cd /path/to/claude-cookbooks/skills' without ever mentioning that the directory is a GitHub repo they must clone first. First-time users hit a dead end with no indication of the missing setup step.
aliases: onboarding block: clone step not documented
skills introduction broken for new users
signals.review_reason: Explicitly labeled 'bug' by the reporter; describes a first-time user onboarding block where the prerequisite 'clone the GitHub repo' is missing from the notebook. Users cannot complete the first step of the skills introduction, qualifying as a UX blocking issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG] intro to skills should point at github repo as install prereq
source_issues.evidence: Bug report states users following the notebook instructions have no way to find the 'claude-cookbooks/skills' directory because the prerequisite of cloning the GitHub repo is never mentioned, leaving users frustrated at a dead end.

signals.topic: Telegram MCP 插件静默卡死且不自动重连，需手动重启恢复
signals.summary: Telegram 插件运行时 inbound polling 静默停止：MCP 进程存活、outbound 工具正常，但 inbound 消息不再送达 Claude。重启 bot.start() 循环可修复，但需手动重启 Claude Code。此外，/mcp dialog 或其他插件重新认证后会触发 MCP disconnect，且不会自动重连。
signals.review_reason: 关键功能静默失效：用户感知到'bot 无响应'但无错误日志，需主动排查才发现 inbound 停掉。2 条 issue 分别对应不同触发场景（bot.start() 静默 return 和 /mcp dialog 触发 disconnect），均指向同一个核心问题：MCP 无自动重连机制。每次发生都阻断消息传递，属明显体验下降。

source_issues.title: fix(telegram): retry polling on silent bot.start() resolution
source_issues.evidence: 插件静默卡死：inbound polling 永久停止，outbound 工具仍工作，10 天内 7 次现场复现。仅重启 Claude Code 可恢复。根因为 bot.start() 在非 bot.stop() 路径下 resolve 时 polling-retry 循环被 return 退出。修复 patch 已验证。

source_issues.title: [telegram] MCP disconnects mid-session and does not auto-reconnect after /mcp dialog or other plugin re-auth
source_issues.evidence: 打开 /mcp dialog 或其他插件重新认证后，telegram MCP disconnect，且不会自动重连。用户需手动运行 /reload-plugins 恢复。实时会话中 outbound 通道静默失效，用户在手机上等待不到回复。

signals.topic: iMessage 插件电话号自聊场景下 reply 工具失败 (AppleScript -1728) 且跨设备自聊消息被静默丢弃
signals.summary: iMessage 插件存在两类自聊失败：(1) 电话号格式 GUID 的自聊 reply 失败，AppleScript 返回 -1728 'Can't get chat id'；(2) 跨设备发送的自聊消息因 is_from_me=1 被静默丢弃，无任何日志，用户完全感知不到消息丢失。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：自聊场景下 agent 完全无法响应（1678）或消息静默丢失（1676），用户无感知但功能实质失效。两条 issue 属同类场景不同 bug，合并为同一痛点主题。电话号自聊有完整复现和 patch；跨设备自聊有数据库层面证据。

source_issues.title: imessage: reply tool fails with AppleScript -1728 for phone-number self-chats
source_issues.evidence: 电话号格式自聊 (any;-;+1XXXXXXXXXX) 的 reply 工具每次调用均报错：'Can't get chat id' (-1728)。Agent 收到 inbound 消息并尝试 reply，但每次失败。用户手机上等待不到回复，失败仅在 MCP 日志中可见（非用户主动查看）。

source_issues.title: iMessage: cross-device self-chat messages silently dropped (is_from_me=1 only)
source_issues.evidence: 从其他设备发送的自聊消息（is_from_me=1 且无 is_from_me=0 副本）被无条件丢弃。6 条跨设备消息全部丢失，无日志无信号，chat.db 中有记录但 Claude 不会处理。SELF 集合未包含电话号码导致自聊检测也失效。

signals.topic: ralph-loop stop hook 因 transcript flush race 遗漏 <promise> 标签导致循环运行至 max-iterations
signals.summary: 当 ralph-loop 带 --completion-promise 运行时，Stop hook 在读取 transcript 时存在竞态条件：Claude 的最终文本块尚未 flush 完毕，导致 hook 遗漏 <promise> 标签，循环直接跑满 max-iterations 而非正常退出。根因为 hook 在 transcript I/O 完成前即被触发，属主流程阻断性 bug。
aliases: ralph-loop promise tag miss race condition
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：循环应正常退出但实际跑满 max-iterations，导致资源浪费和任务超时。有直接 hook-time trace 证据支撑，且 workaround 已验证有效。虽仅 1 条 issue，但为高频使用场景下的阻断性 bug，platform 层已确认根因并关闭 (not planned)，plugin 层需自行修复。

source_issues.title: ralph-loop: stop hook intermittently misses <promise> tag due to transcript flush race (downstream of claude-code#15813)
source_issues.evidence: Stop hook 读取 transcript 时遗漏 <promise> 标签，导致循环运行至 max-iterations。Hook-time trace 直接观察到 race window：fire #2 pre-sleep 无 promise，post-sleep 有 +1238 bytes 新 flush 内容。Workaround (sleep 1.5) 验证有效但引入额外延迟且非根本修复。

signals.topic: skill-creator 在 Windows 上完全无法运行 (select.select 管道不兼容 + cp1252 编码崩溃)
signals.summary: skill-creator 的 run_loop 在所有 Windows 用户机器上完全失败：两个独立 bug 连续触发——select.select 在 Windows 不支持管道导致 100% 查询失败；cp1252 编码写入 ✗ 字符崩溃。约 1/3 开发者受影响，脚本在 iteration 1 即崩溃无法完成任何优化。
signals.review_reason: 主流程完全阻断：Windows 用户（占约 1/3 开发者）skill-creator 根本无法使用，在 iteration 1 即崩溃。虽仅 1 条 issue，但影响用户基数大且失败完全性高，review_reason 给出强用户影响证据，满足 P0 硬约束例外条件。

source_issues.title: skill-creator: run_loop fails on Windows (select.select on pipes + cp1252 encoding)
source_issues.evidence: 所有 Windows 用户 100% 失败：select.select 在 Windows 仅支持 socket，管道触发 WinError 10038；cp1252 编码写入 ✗ 字符触发 UnicodeEncodeError。约 1/3 开发者用户群被完全阻断。两条 patch 均已本地验证可解决。

signals.topic: chat_messages 工具嵌入 HEIC 图片时 API 返回 400 后无限重试导致 agent 挂起无法恢复
signals.summary: iMessage chat_messages 工具自动将附件嵌入消息内容：HEIC 格式图片超出 API 支持范围后触发 400 错误，工具陷入无限重试循环（无错误日志暴露给调用方），agent 界面显示 tool call 进行中但无进展，持续 12 分钟直至外部手动重启。HEIC 是 iPhone 默认截图格式，高度可能反复触发。
aliases: agent stuck on HEIC image embed
signals.review_reason: Agent 不可恢复挂起：典型 iPhone 截图（HEIC 格式）触发后 agent 持续挂起 12 分钟，需外部手动重启。无错误日志暴露，无法通过 agent 自身诊断恢复。HEIC 是 iPhone 默认格式，高度可能反复出现。虽仅 1 条 issue，但 12 分钟不可恢复挂起 + iPhone 高频场景构成强用户影响证据。

source_issues.title: `chat_messages` should support text-only mode (or fail-fast on attachment fetch) to bypass auto-embedded image fetches that 400-and-loop
source_issues.evidence: 2026-04-26 17:38-17:50 BST，12 分钟 agent 挂起直到外部重启。iPhone HEIC 截图（image/heic，898KB）触发 400 'Could not process image'，工具无错误日志暴露给 agent，进入无限重试循环。Agent 界面显示 in-flight tool call，外部观测到进程健康但无响应。

signals.topic: skill-creator scripts 完全无法在 Windows 原生环境运行（subprocess PATHEXT + select on pipes 双重阻断）
signals.summary: skill-creator 的 run_eval.py 和 run_loop.py 在 Windows 原生 Python 下有 3 个兼容性问题，其中 select.select() 在 Windows 上只能操作 socket 而非管道 FD，导致 run_eval/run_loop/improve_description 三个核心脚本全部阻断，用户无法在 Windows 上完成任何 skill 评估和优化流程。
signals.review_reason: 这是明确的主流程阻断：select.select() 在 Windows 上的平台差异导致 run_eval 全部查询失败，run_loop 和 improve_description 也依赖 eval 数据而连带不可用。用户提供了完整修复方案并验证可用，具备明确用户影响证据（所有查询均立即失败，[WinError 10038]）。

source_issues.title: Windows compatibility: skill-creator scripts fail (subprocess PATHEXT, cp1252 encoding, select on pipes)
source_issues.evidence: Issue 3 (BLOCKING): select.select([process.stdout], [], [], 1.0) raises [WinError 10038]. Cause: Python's select.select() on Windows only operates on sockets, not on subprocess pipe file descriptors. This blocks all of run_eval, run_loop, and improve_description (which depends on eval data). The author confirmed: without this fix, the optimizer cannot evaluate any query on Windows.

signals.topic: docx skill 生成的文档在 Microsoft Word 中报 "unreadable content" 无法正常打开
signals.summary: docx skill 在处理文档时，XML 中存在三类未在 lxml schema 中标记但被 Word 拒绝的问题：(1) <w:t> 内含真实换行符；(2) sectPr 硬编码 rId1/rId2 而非从模板 rels 读取真实 ID；(3) numbering.xml 缺少 w:nsid/w:multiLevelType/w:tmpl。三者都会导致 Word 打开时显示"发现无法读取的内容"，用户文档生成流程实质失败。
signals.review_reason: 主流程阻断：docx skill 生成的文件无法被 Microsoft Word 正常打开（核心使用场景失败）。lxml schema 验证通过但 Word 拒绝，说明 skill 生成的 XML 存在语义错误，用户在不知情的情况下会得到损坏文档，是典型的静默失败。

source_issues.title: docx skill no longer works on Ubuntu 26.04
source_issues.evidence: Three XML bugs cause Microsoft Word to show 'Word found unreadable content' on open. All three bugs passed the lxml schema validator but caused Word to reject the document. The author notes it was working fine with Ubuntu 24.04 with the same template — the skill's output is now silently producing corrupted files.

signals.topic: pdf skill 多页文档表格列位置漂移（pdftotext -layout 每页重新缩放列宽）
signals.summary: pdf skill 依赖 pdftotext -layout 处理无结构表格的 PDF，但该工具会基于每页最宽行重新缩放字符列宽。对于跨页的逻辑表格，每页的相同列会落在不同字符位置，导致跨页表格解析算法失效。用户遇到这类文档（Access 导出、数据字典、自动化报告）时，pdftotext 输出无法直接使用。
signals.review_reason: 影响特定但明确的文档处理失败场景：多页无结构表格 PDF（Access 导出、数据字典等常见类型）是真实使用场景，pdftotext 对跨页表格的处理失效会导致用户在遇到这类文档时提取结果错误。但由于是特定文档类型限制而非通用阻断，定为 P2。

source_issues.title: pdf skill: `pdftotext -layout` column-drift on multi-page positional "tables"
source_issues.evidence: pdftotext -layout rescales character-column widths per page based on the widest line on that page. On multi-page documents, the same logical table column lands at different character positions on different pages, which breaks naive layout-based parsers on continuation pages. The issue affects common document types: Microsoft Access exports, schema/data-dictionary dumps, and many auto-generated reports.

signals.topic: pdf skill 大文档（数千页）内存爆炸导致 OOM 被杀
signals.summary: pdfplumber 对每页缓存解析状态，flush_cache() 需要手动调用。对于超大 PDF（约 3000+ 页），内存随页数线性增长，最终触发 OOM 被系统杀死。用户在高页数文档场景下无法完成提取任务。
signals.review_reason: 大文档场景下明确的功能不可用：pdfplumber 缓存机制未在 skill 中说明，导致用户在处理大 PDF 时进程被 OOM 杀死，任务无法完成。虽然是特定场景，但大文档处理是 PDF 工具的合理使用场景。

source_issues.title: pdf skill: `pdftotext -layout` column-drift on multi-page positional "tables"
source_issues.evidence: pdfplumber caches per-page parse state, so without explicit cache flushing memory grows linearly and the process gets OOM-killed (we hit this at ~3000 pages of a 5500-page document). Workaround requires calling page.flush_cache() per page.

signals.topic: skill-creator UnicodeEncodeError：Windows cp1252 编码无法写入报告中的特殊字符
signals.summary: skill-creator 脚本在 Windows 上使用 Path.write_text() 写入 HTML/Markdown 报告时，默认使用 cp1252 编码，无法处理报告中使用的 '✗' 等特殊字符，导致 UnicodeEncodeError，报告文件写入失败。
signals.review_reason: 报告生成失败：eval 报告写入时因特殊字符编码问题崩溃，用户无法获得评估结果。虽然仅影响 Windows 环境，但 skill-creator 的核心输出（报告）无法生成，属于明显体验下降。

source_issues.title: Windows compatibility: skill-creator scripts fail (subprocess PATHEXT, cp1252 encoding, select on pipes)
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeEncodeError: 'charmap' codec can't encode character '✗' in position 10183. Path.write_text() on Windows defaults to cp1252 which cannot encode characters used in eval reports.

signals.topic: MCP OAuth/DCR authentication flows fail, blocking provider and extension setup
signals.summary: MCP OAuth authentication fails in two distinct scenarios: (a) DCR (Dynamic Client Registration) OAuth in WSL — Goose Desktop cannot open a browser for authorization, causing the conversation to hang permanently on DCR-protected MCP server registration; (b) Gemini OAuth onboarding — OAuth flow succeeds in browser but the provider is never added because Goose always sends FREE tier to Google's Code Assist API even for Pro/Advanced accounts, triggering 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT. Both issues block core provider and extension setup workflows.
aliases: MCP server registration hangs on OAuth
signals.review_reason: Two separate OAuth flow failures both result in complete inability to set up critical integrations (MCP extensions and Gemini provider). The DCR issue freezes the entire conversation; the Gemini issue silently fails to add a provider. Both have concrete error traces and workarounds that confirm the account/server is functioning. count=2 meets P1 criteria, and the user impact is clear and blocking even if the absolute user base is moderate.

source_issues.title: Goose desktop in WSL hangs when registering a DCR MCP server
source_issues.evidence: When registering a DCR OAuth-protected MCP server in WSL, Goose Desktop fails to open the authorization browser URL and hangs — the entire conversation becomes unresponsive with no recovery. Workaround of using CLI instead is available but not usable in Desktop context.

source_issues.title: Gemini OAuth flow fails for Gemini Pro/Advanced accounts (400 Bad Request: INVALID_ARGUMENT)
source_issues.evidence: OAuth flow completes in browser but provider is never added. Server logs confirm Goose always sends 'tier: FREE' to Google's onboarding API regardless of actual account tier, causing 400 rejection. API Key method works fine with the same Pro account, proving the account itself is valid. Blocks paid Gemini users from using OAuth-based authentication.

signals.topic: Windows: Goose never cleans up resources — 350GB disk leak + orphaned MCP processes
signals.summary: Three interrelated resource leaks on Windows: (1) MCP child processes spawned via uvx are never terminated on session end or app restart, accumulating as zombie processes; (2) LLM request logs grow quadratically (each turn logs full conversation history), causing 100-150GB over 5 months; (3) temp directories from shell/tool execution in %TEMP% are never cleaned up, adding another 50-100GB. Combined, this consumed ~350GB over 7 months on a single 500GB laptop.
signals.review_reason: This is a massive, quantified disk and memory resource leak on Windows that directly causes application unusability over time (350GB consumed on 500GB drive). All three sub-leaks are confirmed by the same reporter with detailed math. The orphaned MCP process leak additionally causes session instability as zombie processes accumulate. P0 criteria met: severe user impact (disk full = app can't function), no user-level workaround short of manual cleanup scripts, and affects a major OS platform (Windows).

source_issues.title: [Windows] Goose never cleans up after itself — ~350GB disk leak over 7 months
source_issues.evidence: User reports ~350GB disk consumption over 7 months from 3 sources: orphaned MCP processes (~900MB RAM after 1 day, 41 zombie processes), quadratic LLM request log growth (100-150GB over 5 months), and uncleared temp directories (~50-100GB). Entirely blocks the application from being usable long-term on affected Windows machines.

signals.topic: Manually edited config.yaml is silently rolled back on restart, breaking custom MCP extensions
signals.summary: On restart, Goose's configuration self-check mechanism silently overwrites manually edited config.yaml, wiping out any custom MCP extension entries that were not added through the UI. This directly breaks user-configured MCP extensions on every restart, forcing users to re-add them manually each time or find workarounds like symlinking the config directory.
signals.review_reason: Although count=1, this is a direct, reproducible workflow blocker: custom MCP extensions (a core Goose feature) become unavailable after every single restart. The issue is well-characterized with an identified root cause (config self-check mechanism). The workaround (symlink) requires non-standard system configuration. This is not a rare edge case — it affects any user who customizes their config, which is a core use case. P1 is warranted given severity and repeatability.

source_issues.title: Silent Rollback of Manually Edited config.yaml on Restart Breaks Custom MCP Extensions
source_issues.evidence: User reports config directory redirected via mklink to D: drive; manually added MCP extension entries in config.yaml are silently wiped on every restart. The configuration self-check mechanism is identified as the cause. Workaround is to use symlinks, but this is not a normal user action. Custom MCP extensions become unavailable after every restart, breaking a core extensibility feature.

signals.topic: Windows MCP extension environment variable values not read from system, blocking extension setup
signals.summary: On Windows, MCP extension environment variables defined in the Windows system environment (such as API keys and tokens needed by MCP servers) are not read or recognized by Goose Desktop. Users cannot set extension credentials via the Windows environment — the values are silently ignored in the UI, and extensions fail to start with 'Configuration value not found' errors.
aliases: Windows environment variables not read for MCP extensions
MCP extension secret retrieval fails on Windows
signals.review_reason: MCP extensions on Windows cannot use standard environment variable credential management, forcing users to hardcode secrets in config files — a security anti-pattern. This is a workflow blocker for MCP extension setup on Windows, which is a primary Goose use case. While count=1, the issue is reproducible and affects the core extension ecosystem on Windows, a major platform.

source_issues.title: Win11 Goose desktop Extension(MCP): values of Environment Variables cannot be retrieved by system?
source_issues.evidence: User sets WP_API_URL and JWT_TOKEN environment variables in Windows system settings for WooCommerce MCP extension. Goose Desktop UI saves them as empty strings in config.yaml, and the extension fails to start with 'Configuration value not found'. The only workaround is manually editing config.yaml with hardcoded values. This blocks standard Windows credential management for MCP extensions.

signals.topic: Segmentation fault crashes CLI when run over remote SSH session without display
signals.summary: Running goose CLI commands (e.g., goose configure) over a remote SSH session causes a segmentation fault. This occurs because the process tries to initialize a UI/X display that doesn't exist in a headless remote environment, and crashes instead of falling back to CLI mode.
aliases: goose crashes in headless remote session
X11 display error on remote CLI
signals.review_reason: CLI segfault over SSH is a real crash that blocks remote workflow usage, but count=1 and it affects a specific remote-access scenario (SSH with no display). This is a startup crash that makes goose completely unusable in the affected context. P2 rather than P1 because the absolute scope is narrow (headless remote CLI) — most CLI users have a local terminal.

source_issues.title: Segmentation fault (core dumped) on remote cli usage
source_issues.evidence: User runs goose configure via SSH on a remote Ubuntu 24 machine. Process immediately segfaults with 'Missing X server or $DISPLAY' error. The crash occurs because goose initializes its UI layer even in CLI-only usage contexts, rather than detecting headless environments. The .deb-installed binary cannot be used for any CLI operations over SSH.

signals.topic: XPath selectors break easily on minor DOM changes, causing action failures and unnecessary retries
signals.summary: Stagehand's reliance on XPaths for element targeting makes element selection brittle. Minor DOM changes (e.g., new wrapper divs, reordered elements) invalidate cached XPaths, triggering re-inference from the LLM and causing action failures even when the target element is still present.
signals.review_reason: Issue #1555 documents real user impact: XPath brittleness causes action failures and LLM re-inference on minor DOM changes, disrupting the observe/act workflow. While the feature was implemented (PR #1556 closed the issue), the underlying selector reliability problem represents a real, documented pain point affecting browser automation workflows.

source_issues.title: Support Stable Selectors (IDs, Data Attributes, CSS)
source_issues.evidence: Issue explicitly documents that XPaths break on minor DOM changes (new wrapper divs, reordered elements), breaking ActCache and requiring LLM re-inference. Referenced issue #1434 further corroborates XPath brittleness causing action failures.

signals.topic: 子agent调用失败：System message must be at the beginning (API 400)
signals.summary: 子agent调用时后端消息拼接顺序错误，导致LLM API返回400错误'系统消息必须在开头'，子agent任务直接中断。
signals.review_reason: 子agent是DeerFlow的核心工作流组件，子agent调用失败直接导致用户的多步骤复杂任务（如专利研究中的并行子任务）完全中断。日志证据完整（HTTP 400、系统消息顺序错误），影响明确属于主流程阻断级别。

source_issues.title: 子agent调用报错
source_issues.evidence: 用户报告子agent执行时报错 'System message must be at the beginning'，HTTP 400 BadRequestError。开发者确认后端代码中子agent的message拼接顺序有问题，24条消息拼接后system message不在首位。子agent任务完全失败，主流程被阻断。

signals.topic: Docker/NAS部署环境下ASCII编码无法处理非ASCII字符导致LLM请求失败
signals.summary: 在NAS的Docker环境下部署时，非ASCII字符（如中文）导致'ascii' codec can't encode characters错误，所有LLM请求被阻断。
signals.review_reason: 该问题在非英语环境（如中国用户使用飞书集成）中直接阻断所有LLM调用，属于主流程失败。非ASCII编码问题广泛存在于Docker容器化部署场景，用户影响明确（有2条评论确认影响）。

source_issues.title: LLM request failed: 'ascii' codec can't encode characters
source_issues.evidence: 用户在NAS的Docker环境下部署后，与飞书对话中提示 'ascii' codec can't encode characters in position 133-134: ordinal not in range(128)，LLM请求失败。开发者确认是Python默认编码问题导致非ASCII字符无法被正确处理。

signals.topic: 容器沙箱执行长任务时120秒无输出被误判为无输出，任务被跳过
signals.summary: 容器沙箱执行耗时脚本时，120秒内无任何打印内容则被agent判定为任务无输出而直接跳过，但实际上脚本仍在执行。
signals.review_reason: 容器沙箱是DeerFlow代码执行的核心基础设施，120秒无输出即被误判会导致用户执行数据处理、模型训练等长时间任务时结果完全丢失，属于关键功能不可用级别的用户痛点。

source_issues.title: [runtime] 容器沙箱连续120s代码无输出会被agent认为整个任务无输出，但实际任务还在执行
source_issues.evidence: 用户使用容器沙箱执行耗时脚本，120秒后agent认为任务没有输出而直接跳过，但脚本实际还在执行。有日志证据显示命令执行被过早终止（132750 -> 132951，共201秒但被提前处理）。该bug导致长时间运行任务结果丢失。

signals.topic: K8s provisioner未适配userid场景，extra_mounts参数未被消费导致挂载失败
signals.summary: K8s provisioner代码未使用extra_mounts参数，导致需要用户级存储挂载时挂载失败，K8s部署环境下的沙箱功能不可用。
signals.review_reason: K8s是生产级部署标准，provisioner的extra_mounts未消费直接导致需要用户级隔离的沙箱功能完全不可用，阻断K8s生产环境使用。代码证据明确。

source_issues.title: provisioner 根本没有适配 userid的场景，extra_mounts根本没有被消费
source_issues.evidence: 用户提供代码证据显示 _provisioner_create 方法接收 extra_mounts 参数但从未使用，POST请求体中不包含该参数，导致K8s环境下需要用户级挂载时直接失败，沙箱创建不完整。

signals.topic: Nginx本地开发模式因权限问题启动失败（error.log Permission denied）
signals.summary: 本地开发模式下Nginx因无法写入/var/log/nginx/error.log而启动失败，用户无法完成make dev启动全栈开发环境。
aliases: 本地开发 Nginx启动失败
signals.review_reason: make dev是本地开发的唯一入口，Nginx启动失败直接导致全栈开发环境不可用，属于开发体验阻断级问题。新用户首次上手和日常开发均受影响，影响范围覆盖所有非root本地开发环境。

source_issues.title: Nginx failed to start when run in local development mode
source_issues.evidence: 用户执行make dev后，Nginx在等待10秒后仍无法启动，日志显示 'open() /var/log/nginx/error.log failed (13: Permission denied)'，全栈开发环境无法启动。

signals.topic: Invalid schema for 'run_commands' blocks all command execution in beta CLI
signals.summary: Beta CLI returns 'Invalid schema for function run_commands: schema must be a JSON Schema of type object, got type null' across multiple providers (DeepSeek, OpenAI Codex), completely blocking the agent from executing any commands.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow completely blocked. The agent cannot execute any commands, making the entire beta product unusable for any real task. Two independent reports from different providers (DeepSeek, OpenAI Codex) confirm the same root issue.

source_issues.title: Invalid schema error
source_issues.evidence: DeepSeek API + Act Mode: 'Invalid schema for function run_commands: schema must be a JSON Schema of type object, got type null'. Simple task failed.

source_issues.title: Beta Version does not complete any commands
source_issues.evidence: OpenAI Codex GPT 5.4: 'Invalid schema for function run_commands: schema must be a JSON Schema of type object, got type None'. 7 comments with no resolution.

signals.topic: Beta CLI crashes on CPUs without AVX2 support (Illegal instruction)
signals.summary: clite CLI crashes with 'Illegal instruction (core dumped)' on Intel Sandy Bridge CPUs (i5-2500) and older processors lacking AVX2, making the entire CLI unusable on affected hardware.
signals.review_reason: Main flow startup crash on affected hardware. The CLI is completely unusable — cannot be invoked at all. On Windows outside WSL, no error message is shown, making diagnosis even harder.

source_issues.title: Clite not run on WSL on Intel Sandy Bridge Processor (AVX 2 lack)
source_issues.evidence: Pre-compiled npm package for modern AVX2 CPUs fails on i5-2500 Sandy Bridge. Error: 'Illegal instruction (core dumped)'. No workaround available.

signals.topic: Beta clite resume command fails with 'Hub connection closed' causing total workspace state loss
signals.summary: Running 'cline resume' on an existing workspace immediately fails with 'Hub connection closed', all tool calls return 'Invalid input', and session is aborted with 'aborted by another client'. All workspace context (files, git state, command history, agent memory) is lost.
signals.review_reason: Severe session state loss. The entire purpose of the CLI's resume feature is negated — users lose all accumulated workspace context and must rebuild from scratch, representing a major productivity regression.

source_issues.title: clite resume fails with 'Hub connection closed' and 'Invalid input' — total workspace state loss
source_issues.evidence: Resume command fails, all tool calls return 'Invalid input', workspace context completely lost, user must manually reconstruct state from scratch.

signals.topic: CLI terminal freezes when listing MCP servers after cancelling add operation
signals.summary: After entering 'clite mcp' → 'add server' and pressing Ctrl+C to cancel, navigating to 'list servers' freezes the terminal completely. The only recovery is closing and restarting the entire terminal session.
signals.review_reason: Critical workflow disruption. The MCP management flow renders the terminal unusable until fully restarted, losing any ongoing work in that terminal session. This is a reproducibility-tested hard crash with no graceful recovery.

source_issues.title: Terminal freezes if you list MCP servers after cancelling an add server operation
source_issues.evidence: Cancelling add server operation then listing servers causes complete terminal freeze requiring hard restart of terminal.

signals.topic: search_codebase tool emits invalid JSON causing tool failures in agent workflow
signals.summary: search_codebase tool returns 'Tool call arguments could not be parsed as JSON' errors during agent execution. After failure, the LLM abandons the tool and switches to alternative approaches instead of fixing the JSON output, disrupting the intended workflow.
signals.review_reason: Core agent tool repeatedly fails mid-workflow. The search_codebase tool is a fundamental capability for codebase analysis, and its intermittent failure causes the agent to abandon its planned approach, degrading autonomous task completion.

source_issues.title: Agent can't reliably use the search_codebase tool
source_issues.evidence: search_codebase returns 'emitted invalid JSON arguments' error. LLM stops using the tool and pivots to different approaches. Reproduced across 4 attempts.

signals.topic: AI edit desync: follow-up to edit suggestion causes file state mismatch and broken diffs
signals.summary: When AI suggests a code edit and user responds with a follow-up instead of accepting/rejecting, Continue marks the edit as accepted but does not apply it, causing AI to have a desynchronized view of the file. For longer files, subsequent AI diffs fail to apply due to the mismatch.
aliases: follow-up on edit causes state desync
AI edit not applied but marked accepted
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine workflow-blocking bug. When user responds to an AI edit suggestion with a follow-up instead of explicit accept/reject, the edit is silently dropped but the UI falsely signals acceptance. The AI then operates on stale file state, producing diffs that fail to apply. This directly disrupts the core edit workflow and wastes user time with failed operations. Single issue (count=1) but clear user impact and reproducible steps provided.

source_issues.title: Responding with a follow-up when AI suggests an edit results in desync
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with full reproduction steps. When user responds to an edit suggestion with a follow-up, the edit is NOT carried out but the UI marks it as accepted. AI's view of the file disagrees with actual state. For longer files, subsequent diffs fail to apply. Reproducible with DeepSeek Coder on Windows 11.

signals.topic: Model response crash: "Headers is not a constructor" causes message send failure with Gemini 3.1 Pro
signals.summary: When using Gemini 3.1 Pro model, Continue crashes with 'Headers is not a constructor' error when handling the model response, blocking the user from sending messages.
aliases: Headers is not a constructor crash
signals.review_reason: This is a crash that prevents the core messaging workflow from functioning. The 'Headers is not a constructor' error indicates a JavaScript type mismatch, likely a Node.js/fetch API version incompatibility. The error directly blocks users from sending messages with Gemini 3.1 Pro, which is a key supported model. Single issue but clear user-blocking evidence with screenshot.

source_issues.title: Error handling model response: Headers is not a constructor
source_issues.evidence: Bug report with screenshot evidence. User encounters 'Headers is not a constructor' error when Continue attempts to handle the model response from Gemini 3.1 Pro. Error appears in error output panel. User is blocked from continuing the conversation.

signals.topic: CLI onboarding repeatedly prompts even when valid ~/.continue/config.yaml already exists
signals.summary: The Continue CLI (cn) prompts for onboarding/login on every startup even when a complete and valid config.yaml already exists at ~/.continue/config.yaml, forcing users to manually create a .onboarding_complete flag as a workaround.
aliases: CLI repeatedly prompts for onboarding despite existing config
signals.review_reason: This is a workflow-blocking CLI usability issue. Every 'cn' invocation greets users with unwanted onboarding prompts despite a perfectly valid config.yaml being present. The root cause is clearly identified in the source code (runOnboardingFlow checks .onboarding_complete but not config.yaml existence). While there is a workaround, it is non-obvious and represents friction for all CLI users who already have a working config. The bug author confirmed it reproduces on multiple machines.

source_issues.title: CLI: onboarding prompts even when ~/.continue/config.yaml already exists
source_issues.evidence: Detailed bug report with root cause analysis in source code. User with a valid local LLM config (no API key needed) is greeted with onboarding prompts on every 'cn' invocation. The root cause is identified in extensions/cli/src/onboarding.ts:138 - runOnboardingFlow checks for .onboarding_complete flag but not for existing config.yaml. Workaround: 'touch ~/.continue/.onboarding_complete'. Affects multiple machines. Author provided proposed fix with code.

signals.topic: CLI does not auto-discover MCP servers from .continue/mcpServers/ directory unlike IDE
signals.summary: The Continue CLI (cn) does not auto-discover MCP server config files placed in .continue/mcpServers/, despite official docs recommending this as the quick-start approach and the IDE extensions supporting it. Users following docs get no tools and no error.
aliases: MCP servers not found in CLI despite being in docs
signals.review_reason: This is a CLI/IDE parity gap that breaks the documented quick-start workflow. Users who follow the official docs for MCP server setup get zero tools when using the CLI, with no error or feedback to explain why. The IDE correctly discovers these files. This creates silent failure that users may not immediately understand, forcing them to fall back to editing global config.yaml. Count=1 (single repo) so P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: CLI: auto-discover MCP servers in .continue/mcpServers/ like the IDE does
source_issues.evidence: Enhancement request with detailed technical analysis. The IDE already supports scanning ~/.continue/mcpServers/*.json and <workspaceDir>/.continue/mcpServers/*.json, but the CLI only reads from config.yaml and command-line flags. Users following the official quick-start docs (which describe dropping YAML files into .continue/mcpServers/) see no tools and no error when using 'cn'. This creates a surprise factor and breaks documented workflow.

signals.topic: Tracing disabled info message repeatedly printed with no suppression option
signals.summary: When tracing is disabled, CrewAI repeatedly prints a verbose 'Info: Tracing is disabled.' message (reported 100+ times per run) with no environment variable or flag to suppress it. The has_user_declined_tracing() check produces the same output regardless of its result.
aliases: tracing disabled message cannot be suppressed
signals.review_reason: Repeated noisy output in every crew run degrades user experience significantly. While not technically blocking the main output, it pollutes logs and console during every execution, requiring users to filter out this spam. Count=1 within this dataset but clearly a user pain point as evidenced by the repeated printing bug.

source_issues.title: [BUG] I can not stop the "Info: Tracing is disabled." nagging.
source_issues.evidence: User reports the message appears 100 times per run with screenshot evidence. Both has_user_declined_tracing() branches produce identical output, making suppression logic broken.

signals.topic: OpenAI API key fails with 401 inside CrewAI despite working in standalone tests
signals.summary: A valid OpenAI API key tested successfully with Python OpenAI client and curl fails with 401 'Incorrect API key provided' when executed inside CrewAI via crew.kickoff(). Logs show repeated auth failures and VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch warnings, suggesting CrewAI does not correctly propagate environment variables to its subprocess runtime.
aliases: OPENAI_API_KEY not propagated to CrewAI runtime
API key works outside CrewAI but fails inside
signals.review_reason: Blocks the primary workflow (crew.kickoff) for users with correctly configured API keys. The key issue is that CrewAI's subprocess isolation does not preserve environment variables, causing 401 auth failures at the LLM layer. Full stack trace and reproduction steps confirm this is a CrewAI-specific propagation bug, not a key configuration issue.

source_issues.title: [BUG] OpenAI API key works locally but fails inside CrewAI with 401 invalid_api_key
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace showing openai.AuthenticationError 401. VIRTUAL_ENV mismatch warning: '/data/internal/venv does not match the project environment path /shared_venv'. Subprocess launches isolated venv, losing the env var. Tools validate successfully but LLM calls fail. Multiple retries shown in logs.

signals.topic: OpenRouter thinking models (Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Gemini 3.1) cause 'Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty' crash
signals.summary: When using OpenRouter with thinking models (anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-5, anthropic/claude-opus-4-5, or google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview), CrewAI crashes with ValueError: 'Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty.' at handle_max_iterations_exceeded, instead of the same models working correctly via GLM, Qwen, or GPT.
aliases: LLM returns None with thinking models
signals.review_reason: Blocks a specific class of model providers (OpenRouter thinking models) that users deliberately choose for advanced capabilities. Full stack trace shows the crash is in CrewAI's task execution path (execute_task -> _invoke_loop_native_tools -> handle_max_iterations_exceeded), not in the LLM provider itself. Users lose access to high-quality thinking models with no workaround.

source_issues.title: [BUG] Problems with OpenRouter thinking models
source_issues.evidence: Full 27-frame stack trace ending in ValueError: Invalid response from LLM call - None or empty. Screenshots of error responses from OpenRouter. Multiple thinking models affected (Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview). Same setup works with non-thinking models (GLM, Qwen, GPT). Academic writing workflow is blocked.

signals.topic: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ triggers blocking LLM call at module import, crashes containers before HTTP server starts
signals.summary: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ calls generate_crew_chat_inputs which triggers synchronous blocking LLM calls (generate_input_description_with_ai, generate_crew_description_with_ai) at module import time, before uvicorn binds to the HTTP port. Any LLM hiccup (500, 503, rate-limit, timeout, invalid credentials) causes the Python process to exit with code 1, making the deployed service completely unreachable.
aliases: LLM call at import time crashes container
container crash on LLM error at startup
signals.review_reason: Critical production deployment blocker. Any LLM provider issue during container startup (common: rate limits, transient errors, cold-start delays) causes the entire service to fail unrecoverably before it can serve any traffic. The container becomes completely unreachable, and orchestrators (Railway, Kubernetes, ECS, Fly.io) roll back the deployment. No timeout, retry, or fallback exists in the code path. P0 because it defeats the entire purpose of a deployed service.

source_issues.title: ChatWithCrewFlow.__init__ makes blocking LLM call at module import, crashes containers on any LLM hiccup
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace from real Railway deployment. Container exits code 1 before binding port. Orchestrator health check fails and deploy rolls back. The fix requires monkey-patching private functions as a workaround. Affects all production deployments using ag_ui_crewai with CopilotKit.

signals.topic: JSON detection regex misidentifies GraphQL schemas and non-JSON curly-brace content as JSON, causing Task output_pydantic to fail
signals.summary: In crewai.utilities.converter, _JSON_PATTERN = re.compile(r'({.*})', re.DOTALL) naively matches any curly-brace content as JSON. This causes GraphQL schemas (which use curly braces but are not JSON) to be extracted and passed to pydantic.model_validate_json, resulting in ValidationError and blocking task completion for any workflow using output_pydantic with GraphQL-like content.
aliases: incorrect JSON extraction breaks structured output
signals.review_reason: Blocks task completion for users with output_pydantic whose LLM output contains any curly-brace content that is not valid JSON. The bug is in CrewAI's JSON extraction logic, which is fundamentally too greedy. However, count=1 in this dataset and the false-positive scenario (GraphQL, YAML snippets, etc.) is an edge case rather than a common primary workflow. P2 is appropriate.

source_issues.title: [BUG] when using Task(..., output_pydantic=MyModel) some JSON substring identification within the data occurs with possible false positive
source_issues.evidence: Full stack trace showing pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: Invalid JSON: key must be a string. User is using an MCP server to fetch GraphQL schemas and needs to return them as strings via output_pydantic=GraphQLSchema. The regex matches the entire GraphQL schema as JSON, then fails validation.

signals.topic: Claude Opus model temperature parameter deprecated causing API 400 errors

aliases: temperature parameter API error on Opus
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow failure: the temperature parameter causes 400 errors that completely block all pattern executions when using the Opus model. While only 1 issue, the error is reproducible and directly prevents user workflows from completing. This qualifies as P1 because the count is 1 but the impact is workflow-blocking for Opus users.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Opus-4.7 temperature deprecated for this model
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 Bad Request: '`temperature` is deprecated for this model.' Full workflow blocked — any Fabric pattern using Opus model fails with this error.

signals.topic: Groq API rejects messages array when last role is 'system' instead of 'user', breaking built-in patterns
signals.summary: Fabric's Groq vendor adapter sends chat payloads where the last message role is 'system' (when pattern INPUT is placed in system.md). Groq's chat.completions API rejects these with 'last message role must be user', breaking multiple built-in patterns like summarize when using the Groq provider.
aliases: Groq vendor last role must be user
signals.review_reason: This is a main flow failure for Groq users: built-in patterns like summarize break with 400 errors because the Groq API requires the last message role to be 'user'. The issue explicitly states 'many built-in patterns' are affected, not just one. The adapter fails to adapt the message format for the Groq API contract, directly blocking user workflows when using the Groq vendor.

source_issues.title: Groq chat.completions rejects Fabric payload when pattern input becomes a system message (last role must be 'user')
source_issues.evidence: API returns 400 Bad Request: 'last message role must be user'. Demonstrated with built-in 'summarize' pattern. Multiple built-in patterns are affected since many place the INPUT marker in system.md by design. Full workflow blocked for all Groq users.

signals.topic: CLI crashes with ENAMETOOLONG error when pasting long strings (stack traces, log files) into prompt

aliases: ENAMETOOLONG crash on long pasted text
CLI crashes when pasting stack traces
parseAllAtCommands treats long strings as file paths
signals.review_reason: Clear root cause in input parser. Common user scenario (pasting stack traces or log excerpts) causes unhandled CLI crash. 3 comments indicating active engagement. The bug blocks the core use case of pasting content for analysis.

source_issues.title: CLI crashes with ENAMETOOLONG when pasting long strings into prompt
source_issues.evidence: parseAllAtCommands identifies strings starting with @ as file paths and passes to resolveToRealPath which calls fs.lstatSync without validating length. When string exceeds OS max path length (e.g., 1024 on macOS), ENAMETOOLONG is thrown and crashes CLI with unhandled promise rejection.

source_issues.evidence: During high-volume shell command execution across large workspace with thousands of files, CLI returns 'Too many open files' error (Exit Code 126). Subsequent shell commands fail with forkpty(3) failed. Session becomes unusable without restart.

signals.topic: Symlinked SKILL.md crashes agent and error message is hidden
signals.summary: FilesystemBackend re-raises bare OSError (e.g. OSError(ELOOP) from symlinked SKILL.md) which breaks SkillsMiddleware (enabled by default in CLI), causing every agent invocation to abort. The underlying error (e.g. 'Too many levels of symbolic links') is stripped by langgraph_api/serde.py, leaving only 'An internal error occurred'. Combined with the log-hiding bug (#3012), users have zero visibility into the root cause.
signals.review_reason: 3 distinct issues all referencing the same root cause: bare OSError from symlink handling propagates out of FilesystemBackend, SkillsMiddleware (default in CLI) crashes, and the error is stripped to 'An internal error occurred'. Affects macOS users with symlinked skill directories (Claude Code's default layout). This blocks the primary agent startup flow.

source_issues.title: FilesystemBackend re-raises bare OSError, breaks SkillsMiddleware on symlinked SKILL.md

source_issues.title: Virtual path execution issue with CompositeBackend
source_issues.evidence: Original issue on same root cause as #3050: execute() receives literal virtual paths that don't exist as OS paths.

signals.topic: SubAgentMiddleware IndexError crash when subagent returns empty messages list
signals.summary: _run_subagent() crashes with IndexError at subagents.py line 411 when result['messages'] is an empty list. Any subagent that exits without emitting messages (early graph exit, tool-only subagent) crashes the parent agent.
signals.review_reason: 2 confirmed reports of the same crash in SubAgentMiddleware core code path. Subagents are a core deepagents feature. Any subagent that finishes without emitting messages (early graph exit, tool-only subagent) crashes the parent agent. The fix is trivial (1-line guard) but the crash is real and reproducible.

source_issues.title: `IndexError` in `SubAgentMiddleware` when LLM returns empty messages
source_issues.evidence: result['messages'][-1].text.rstrip() raises IndexError when messages list is empty. Reproducer included. Crashes _run_subagent at line 411.

source_issues.title: bug(subagents): IndexError when subagent returns empty messages list
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause: _return_command_with_state_update accesses result['messages'][-1] without checking if list is non-empty. Impact: any subagent that exits early crashes parent.

signals.topic: BaseSandbox.read() silently returns base64 instead of text for valid UTF-8 files larger than 8192 bytes with multi-byte characters at boundary
signals.summary: The UTF-8 sniff reads exactly 8192 bytes and uses strict decode. When a multi-byte UTF-8 character straddles byte 8192, the decode fails and the entire valid UTF-8 file is returned as base64. The agent silently receives garbled content. Caused an LLM policy violation in production.
signals.review_reason: 2 confirmed reports of the same silent bug. The agent silently receives base64-encoded content instead of the actual file text, corrupting its input. Reported to have caused an LLM policy violation in production (base64 blob flagged by Anthropic's classifier). Affects any text file >8KB with multi-byte characters, i.e., almost any PDF/Word-extracted content.

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.read() returns base64 for valid UTF-8 files when multi-byte char straddles 8192-byte sniff boundary
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows Korean text file >8192 bytes returns base64 instead of UTF-8 text. Causes LLM policy violation in production when base64 blob was flagged. Agent silently receives garbled content.

source_issues.title: BaseSandbox.read() returns base64 instead of text for valid UTF-8 files when a multi-byte character is split at the prefix boundary
source_issues.evidence: Same bug: multi-byte UTF-8 character split at 8192 boundary causes silent base64 return for valid text files. Minimal reproducer included.
