signals.topic: Long tool calls (~180s) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud, causing 2-3x duplicate work and cost
signals.summary: When a tool call runs longer than ~180 seconds on LangGraph Cloud, it gets silently re-dispatched from the last checkpoint while the original is still running. Both complete successfully, resulting in redundant LLM calls, redundant tool executions, and inflated costs. The underlying cause is a hardcoded 120s heartbeat interval in langgraph-api combined with swept runs being re-queued as retriable.
signals.review_reason: Directly causes 2-3x cost duplication and redundant LLM/tool calls in a production cloud environment. Heartbeat mechanism re-dispatches long-running tasks as retriable, creating silent financial and computational waste. User provided root-cause analysis with evidence across multiple versions.

source_issues.title: Long tool calls (~180s+) silently re-executed from checkpoint on LangGraph Cloud
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed duplicate tool calls with identical arguments appearing ~180s after start; both original and duplicate complete successfully; 2-3x redundant work and cost; persists across langgraph 1.1.3-1.1.6 and multiple Cloud configurations

signals.topic: PostgresSaver.setup() fails inside transactions due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
signals.summary: PostgresSaver.setup() raises ActiveSqlTransaction when called within any explicit transaction because the migration SQL uses CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY, which cannot run inside a transaction block. This blocks atomic provisioning flows where checkpoint table setup must commit or rollback together with schema creation and external bookkeeping.
aliases: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY in transaction block
signals.review_reason: Blocks legitimate atomic provisioning workflows required for multi-tenant deployments. The autocommit workaround is not acceptable because it breaks the transactional semantics users depend on. No clean workaround exists for affected users.

source_issues.title: PostgresSaver.setup() fails when called inside a transaction due to CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY
source_issues.evidence: psycopg.errors.ActiveSqlTransaction raised at setup time; blocks atomic provisioning for schema-per-tenant onboarding; autocommit=True workaround defeats atomicity; also triggered by implicit upstream transaction contexts in LangGraph itself

signals.topic: PostgresStore numeric filter operators use lexicographic comparison instead of numeric, producing silently wrong query results
signals.summary: PostgresStore._get_filter_condition() uses value->>key (text extraction) with str() for $gt/$gte/$lt/$lte operators. Since ->> returns TEXT in PostgreSQL, numeric comparisons use lexicographic ordering ('9' >= '10' is True), causing items with score=2..9 to incorrectly pass filters like $gte: 10. This is a data correctness bug that silently produces wrong query results in production.
signals.review_reason: Silently wrong query results in production PostgreSQL queries — a data correctness bug that affects business logic without raising any error. The same operator pattern works correctly in SqliteStore, indicating a clear regression in the Postgres implementation.

source_issues.title: Bug: PostgresStore numeric filter operators ($gt, $gte, $lt, $lte) use lexicographic (text) comparison instead of numeric comparison
source_issues.evidence: Reproducer shows 'value->>%s > %s' with str param '10' producing wrong ordering; items with score=2..9 incorrectly pass $gte:10 filter; SqliteStore already handles this correctly with CAST(... AS REAL)

signals.topic: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite in concurrent supersteps
signals.summary: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() has a guard 'if not seen_overwrite:' that silently discards values arriving after an Overwrite in the same batch, with no error or warning. In concurrent supersteps, write ordering within apply_writes is determined by path sorting, so regular values from slower tasks can be silently lost when an Overwrite sorts first.
signals.review_reason: Data loss bug in concurrent execution — channel updates are silently dropped with no error. This corrupts graph state in production concurrent workloads without any warning, making debugging extremely difficult.

source_issues.title: bug: BinaryOperatorAggregate.update() silently drops values arriving after Overwrite
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows ch.update([Overwrite(10), 5]) produces 10 instead of expected 15; 5 is silently discarded; no error raised; affects concurrent supersteps where write ordering is path-determined not user-intended

signals.topic: ensure_config mutates shared metadata dict by reference, leaking thread_id across invocations
signals.summary: ensure_config assigns the metadata key by reference without calling .copy(), so configurable values like thread_id get injected into the shared metadata dict of the base config. After the first invocation, subsequent calls see metadata contaminated with data from previous invocations, breaking multi-tenant isolation.
signals.review_reason: Cross-invocation metadata contamination breaks session isolation in multi-tenant scenarios. The shared config dict is mutated by reference, causing thread_id data from one invocation to leak into the base config and affect all subsequent invocations.

source_issues.title: bug: ensure_config mutates shared metadata when copiable keys passed by reference
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction shows original_config metadata dict mutated after ensure_config call; thread_id from new_config appears in original_config metadata; breaks multi-tenant isolation when base config is shared across threads

signals.topic: Workflow file upload API returns 400 'Invalid upload file' in v1.14.0 (regression from v1.13)
signals.summary: After upgrading to v1.14.0, calling POST /v1/workflows/run with any valid file input always returns 400 'Invalid upload file', completely blocking workflows that use file input fields. Separately, the batch file upload limit is hardcoded to 10 regardless of UPLOAD_FILE_BATCH_LIMIT and WORKFLOW_FILE_UPLOAD_LIMIT environment variable settings, silently ignoring the configured limit.
signals.review_reason: Two independent reports confirm file upload is broken in 1.14.0 — one is a full regression (API returns 400 for all file inputs, completely blocking workflows with file inputs), the other is a hardcoded batch limit that silently ignores configured environment variables. Both directly block the primary use case of document processing workflows.

source_issues.title: [1.14.0] API file upload is broken, works fine in 1.13.0
source_issues.evidence: Calling POST /v1/workflows/run with valid file_id (uploaded via /v1/files/upload) always returns 400 'Invalid upload file'. Verified with both object and string format. Regression from 1.13 where same call works.

source_issues.title: File Upload limited to 10 whatever the settings of env variables
source_issues.evidence: Set IMAGE_FILE_BATCH_LIMIT=50, UPLOAD_FILE_BATCH_LIMIT=50, WORKFLOW_FILE_UPLOAD_LIMIT=50 — no warning is shown for >10 files, but workflow only processes 10 files silently, ignoring all environment settings.

signals.topic: online-users API endpoint returns 500 Internal Server Error in v1.14.0 after loading >50 apps
signals.summary: After upgrading to v1.14.0, the /apps/workflows/online-users endpoint fails with 500 Internal Server Error or 400 Bad Request depending on the number of apps loaded. The backend has a hardcoded limit MAX_WORKFLOW_ONLINE_USERS_QUERY_IDS=50, but the frontend does not batch requests, causing errors when workspaces exceed 50 apps.
aliases: workspace with many apps breaks homepage
signals.review_reason: Two reports confirm the online-users endpoint breaks in 1.14.0 (500 for many apps, 400 for >50 apps). The homepage continuously shows Internal Server Error alerts, making the application unusable for any user with a moderately-sized workspace. This is a primary navigation/homepage-level blocker.

source_issues.title: After loading more than 50 apps in a workspace, a bad request error occurred when get workflow online users
source_issues.evidence: Backend has hardcoded MAX_WORKFLOW_ONLINE_USERS_QUERY_IDS=50, but frontend does not batch when >50 apps exist, causing 400 Bad Request on /apps/workflows/online-users.

source_issues.title: [Bug] online-users endpoint broken due to incorrect runtime type error
source_issues.evidence: After upgrading to 1.14.0, /apps/workflows/online-users returns 500 Internal Server Error, causing Internal Server Error alert to keep showing at intervals on the homepage.

signals.topic: Knowledge Base hybrid search silently drops retrieval results for documents with identical text content
signals.summary: When two different documents share identical text sections, the Knowledge Base retrieval deduplication logic (using page_content only as key) collapses them into a single result. The second document's result is silently dropped, breaking citations, attribution, and downstream logic that depends on source metadata.
signals.review_reason: This is a data integrity failure in a core Knowledge Base feature. The retrieval silently drops valid results from second documents with identical text, which directly breaks RAG quality — users get incomplete answers and incorrect citations without any warning. This is not a cosmetic issue but a fundamental accuracy problem.

source_issues.title: Knowledge Base: Duplicate content chunks from different documents are collapsed during retrieval (content-only deduplication ignores metadata)
source_issues.evidence: Two chunks with identical text content but different doc_id UUIDs from different source documents are treated as duplicates — only the first is kept. Any downstream citation or attribution that depends on the second document's metadata is silently lost. Root cause identified in api/core/rag/datasource/retrieval_service.py deduplication logic.

signals.topic: General Chunker plugin returns empty chunks causing embedding pipeline failure
signals.summary: The General Chunker plugin (langgenius/general_chunker v0.0.11) returns empty strings in the chunks array when documents contain consecutive line breaks or sparse content. These empty chunks are passed to the embedding model, causing the indexing pipeline to fail with 'MissingParameter: input[n].text' error (HTTP 400).
aliases: General Chunker empty chunks embedding error
RAG indexing pipeline fails on empty chunks
signals.review_reason: The Chunker producing empty chunks is a reproducible pipeline failure that blocks the entire RAG indexing workflow. Users cannot index documents with common formatting (consecutive line breaks), and the failure provides a cryptic API error rather than a clear user message. This is a core workflow blocker.

source_issues.title: General Chunker returns empty chunks causing embedding failure (MissingParameter: input[n].text)
source_issues.evidence: Documents with consecutive newlines cause the General Chunker to emit empty strings in chunks array, e.g., ['foo bar', '', 'baz', '']. Passing these to the Knowledge Base indexing node triggers embedding error: Error code 400 - MissingParameter, param: input[n].text.

signals.topic: Agent editor cannot be opened in v1.14.0
signals.summary: After upgrading to v1.14.0, attempting to create a new Agent or edit an existing Agent causes the editor page to fail to open. This blocks users from the primary agent creation workflow.
aliases: agent editor page fails to load 1.14.0
signals.review_reason: The Agent editor is a core Dify feature — its complete failure to open after upgrading to 1.14.0 is a primary workflow blocker. Users cannot create or modify agents, which is a fundamental use case of the platform.

source_issues.title: Agent editor cannot open.
source_issues.evidence: Creating a new agent or editing an existing agent results in the editor page failing to open entirely. Reproduced on Docker self-hosted v1.14.0.

signals.topic: Embedding provider switch silently drops all memory writes (vector dimension mismatch)
signals.summary: When users switch the embedding provider via dashboard (e.g. OpenAI → Gemini), the pgvector collection retains the old provider's vector dimension. Memory writes silently fail — API returns success with a memory ID but nothing is persisted. Users lose data with no error indication.
aliases: vector dimension mismatch on embedder change
silent write failure after provider switch
signals.review_reason: Core data loss bug — writes appear to succeed but data is permanently lost with no error. This is a P0 because it silently destroys user data without any indication, directly breaking the primary value proposition of memory persistence.

source_issues.title: bug(server): switching embedding provider silently drops writes due to vector dimension mismatch
source_issues.evidence: API returns success with memory ID but GET /memories returns empty; postgres COUNT(*) = 0. Root cause: pgvector config defaults to 1536 (OpenAI-specific) and ignores actual embedder's embedding_dims.

signals.topic: Dashboard saves stale API key on provider change; .env cannot override database config (unrecoverable locked state)
signals.summary: Two combined bugs trap users in unrecoverable bad state: (1) dashboard pre-populates API key field with old provider's key when switching providers, causing stale key to be saved; (2) once saved to database, .env changes are permanently ignored on restart. Users are locked out with no reset path.
aliases: dashboard provider change saves wrong API key
database config overrides env vars permanently
signals.review_reason: Unrecoverable configuration trap: users who misconfigure their provider via the dashboard are permanently stuck with no escape path. Combined with pp01 (silent data loss), users switching to Gemini or any non-OpenAI provider face cascading unrecoverable failures. High severity P0 despite count=1 due to complete feature destruction with no recovery mechanism.

source_issues.title: bug(server): dashboard saves wrong API key on provider change; .env cannot override database config
source_issues.evidence: After switching provider via dashboard and saving, subsequent memory operations fail with 'API key not valid'. User cannot reset via .env — database overrides permanently win on restart.

signals.topic: Concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index (IndexError on read)
signals.summary: When multiple coroutines call AsyncMemory.add/update/delete concurrently, Qdrant's HNSW index becomes corrupted, producing 'IndexError: index N is out of bounds'. Subsequent reads return wrong results or crash until process restart and index rebuild.
aliases: Qdrant HNSW index corruption under concurrent writes
signals.review_reason: Runtime corruption bug triggered by legitimate concurrent usage (async agents processing events in parallel). Search/get becomes completely broken, requiring process restart and full index rebuild. Impacts any production async agentic system.

source_issues.title: Bug: concurrent AsyncMemory writes corrupt Qdrant HNSW index ('index N is out of bounds')
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction with 20 concurrent asyncio.gather writers produces IndexError. HNSW graph builder is not re-entrant — second writer reading partially-built graph triggers out-of-bounds access.

signals.topic: Memory.search returns score=1.0 for all results (relevance ranking completely broken)
signals.summary: In mem0 2.0.0, Memory.search() returns score=1.0 for every result regardless of actual relevance. The vector store and embedder work correctly in isolation, but the wrapper layer returns identical scores for relevant and irrelevant memories.
signals.review_reason: Core search functionality is completely broken — all results are returned with identical scores, making it impossible for users to distinguish relevant from irrelevant memories. Directly undermines the primary use case of memory retrieval.

source_issues.title: Memory.search returns identical score=1.0 for all results in 2.0.0
source_issues.evidence: Reproduction script shows Thai food memory and server deploy memory both get score=1.0. Direct vector_store.search() call returns correct cosine distances (0.41, 1.32, 1.45), confirming embedder and vector store work correctly.

signals.topic: Self-hosted deployment fails cross-device access (localhost hardcoding)
signals.summary: Self-hosted deployments cannot be accessed from other devices because frontend requests are sent to http://localhost:8888 instead of the server's actual IP. Users following official deployment docs are blocked from using the service on any device other than the host.
aliases: localhost hardcoded in frontend API calls
signals.review_reason: Blocks the primary self-hosted deployment use case — users cannot access the service from any device other than the host machine. Affects the official deployment flow documented in the project's own documentation.

source_issues.title: Some Issues Encountered During Self-Hosted Deployment
source_issues.evidence: User deployed per official docs, accessing from another device shows network error because request goes to localhost:8888 instead of server IP.

signals.topic: Python SDK import failures due to empty __init__.py in agent-framework 1.2.2 breaking all Python imports
signals.summary: agent-framework 1.2.2 ships with empty __init__.py that exports only ['Agent', '__version__'], breaking all meaningful Python imports including foundry integration, semantic kernel tools, and middleware classes. Three separate issues (5609, 5590, 5564) confirm this across different import paths.
signals.review_reason: count=3 meets P0 threshold. All three issues stem from agent-framework 1.2.2 shipping with empty __init__.py which breaks all Python imports across the SDK. Users cannot use foundry integration, semantic kernel tools, or any agent_framework meaningful imports. This is a main workflow blocking issue affecting every Python user of the SDK.

source_issues.title: Python: ImportError: agent-framework-foundry 1.2.2 cannot import AgentMiddlewareLayer from agent-framework 1.2.2
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'AgentMiddlewareLayer' from 'agent_framework'. The class exists in _middleware but is not re-exported from the public __init__.py which only exports ['Agent', '__version__']

source_issues.title: Python [Bug]: ImportError: cannot import name '__version__' from 'agent_framework' — empty __init__.py breaks all imports via observability.py
source_issues.evidence: agent-framework==1.2.2 ships with an empty __init__.py. Nearly every useful import pulls in observability.py which does 'from . import __version__' causing ImportError on first meaningful import

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: ImportError: cannot import name 'AIFunction' from 'agent_framework'
source_issues.evidence: ImportError: cannot import name 'AIFunction' from 'agent_framework' when using semantic-kernel's as_agent_framework_tool() method

signals.topic: GroupChat tool approval workflow crashes with HTTP 400 after approved tool executes
signals.summary: When using GroupChat with ApprovalRequiredAIFunction tools, the workflow crashes with HTTP 400 after the approved tool executes, preventing completion of multi-iteration group chat. System.ClientModel.ClientResultException: HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error: messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceding message with 'tool_calls').
signals.review_reason: Main workflow blocking. When using GroupChat with ApprovalRequiredAIFunction tools, the workflow crashes with HTTP 400 after the approved tool executes, preventing any multi-iteration group chat workflow from completing. This is a complete workflow failure for a key use case.

source_issues.title: .NET: [Bug]: GroupChat tool approval flow causes HTTP 400 — tool message without preceding assistant tool_calls
source_issues.evidence: System.ClientModel.ClientResultException: HTTP 400 (invalid_request_error: ) - Invalid parameter: messages with role 'tool' must be a response to a preceding message with 'tool_calls'. Workflow crashes after tool approval execution, preventing completion of multi-iteration group chat.

signals.topic: FoundryAgent calling Prompt Agent fails with 'Missing required parameter: model' (regression in 1.2.0-1.2.2)
signals.summary: Calling a Prompt Agent via FoundryAgent fails on 1.2.0, 1.2.1, and 1.2.2 with HTTP 400 'Missing required parameter: model'. The same code works correctly on 1.1.1. PR #5447 introduced a regression where agent_reference is no longer attached to extra_body.
signals.review_reason: Regression in 1.2.0-1.2.2 that breaks the primary use case (calling Prompt Agents via FoundryAgent). Works in 1.1.1 but broken in all 1.2.x versions indicates a clear SDK regression affecting production deployments. While count=1, the version range affected (three consecutive releases) and the core functionality broken justify P1.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: FoundryAgent against a Prompt Agent fails with 'Missing required parameter: 'model'' in 1.2.0–1.2.2 (works in 1.1.1)
source_issues.evidence: Calling a Prompt Agent via FoundryAgent fails on 1.2.0, 1.2.1, and 1.2.2 with 400 'Missing required parameter: model'. Same code works on 1.1.1. Suspect PR #5447 introduced regression where agent_reference is no longer attached to extra_body.

signals.topic: Hosted agent deployment fails with HTTP 500 server_error on client.agents.create_version()
signals.summary: Hosted agent deployment to Foundry environment consistently fails with HTTP 500 server_error on create_version() call. HttpResponseError: (server_error) An error occurred while processing your request. This blocks the core deployment workflow for hosted agents.
signals.review_reason: Blocks hosted agent deployment entirely with HTTP 500. Users cannot deploy their agents to Foundry hosted environment, which is a key feature unavailability for production workflows.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: `server_error` on `client.agents.create_version()` for hosted agent — SDK v2.1.0 / agent-framework 1.2.2
source_issues.evidence: HttpResponseError: (server_error) An error occurred while processing your request. HTTP 500 on create_version() consistently prevents hosted agent deployment. Error persists across retries with valid container image.

signals.topic: ResponsesHostServer middleware cannot access request metadata, authorization headers, or trace context (OBO tokens and traceparent unavailable)
signals.summary: Users cannot access Authorization Header (needed for OBO token), x-client-* headers, traceparent header, or metadata in ResponsesHostServer middleware. The old from_agent_framework library provided _request_headers but the new ResponsesHostServer does not expose this data.
signals.review_reason: Blocks key features: users cannot get OAuth tokens for tools or maintain end-to-end traceability via traceparent headers. This is significant experience degradation for production deployments requiring OAuth-protected tools and observability.

source_issues.title: Python: [Bug]: Foundry Hosted Agent Library - Unable to access metadata and client headers
source_issues.evidence: Users cannot access Authorization Header (needed for OBO token), x-client-* headers, traceparent header, or metadata in middleware. The old library (from_agent_framework) provided _request_headers but new ResponsesHostServer does not expose this.

signals.topic: TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext trimming corrupts conversation message ordering, causing tool_result/tool_use_id mismatch errors
signals.summary: When the token-limited context removes elements from the middle of the message history, it can break the adjacency requirement between tool_use and tool_result blocks. This causes downstream API calls to fail with BadRequestError when the LLM receives a tool_result without its corresponding tool_use in the preceding message — breaking multi-step agent workflows in production.
aliases: token trimming breaks tool call ordering
signals.review_reason: This is a confirmed workflow-blocking bug. The token trimming logic removes elements from the middle of the message list, which breaks the required adjacency between tool_use and tool_result message pairs. This causes a BadRequestError that prevents the agent workflow from completing. The error is reproducible and documented with a full stack trace and API error code, indicating this breaks real multi-step agent production workflows.

source_issues.title: TokenLimitedChatCompletionContext removes elements from the middle, which may cause errors in certain situations. Should it remove elements from the beginning of the list rather than from the middle?
source_issues.evidence: Error: openai.BadRequestError with code MPE-001 — 'messages.68.content.1: unexpected tool_use_id found in tool_result blocks: toolu_vrtx_01MCPRK1tTKWRkHW3SxMFGKL. Each tool_result block must have a corresponding tool_use block in the previous message.' Reproducible in production when conversation exceeds token limit.

signals.topic: PlaywrightController fails to read page_script.js in non-UTF-8 environments, crashing MagenticOne on startup
signals.summary: PlaywrightController reads a JavaScript file using the default system encoding instead of UTF-8. In environments with non-UTF-8 code pages (e.g., Windows cp950 for Traditional Chinese), this causes a UnicodeDecodeError that crashes the entire MagenticOne application immediately on startup, making the web surfer agent completely unusable.
aliases: UnicodeDecodeError in PlaywrightController on non-English systems
signals.review_reason: This is a startup crash that renders MagenticOne completely unusable for users in non-English environments. The PlaywrightController.reads page_script.js without specifying encoding='utf-8', causing UnicodeDecodeError on systems using code pages like cp950. The crash occurs immediately on launch, is fully reproducible, and the fix is a one-line change (adding encoding='utf-8'). This directly blocks users from running the web surfer agent on non-English systems.

source_issues.title: open needs encoding='utf-8' for non-english environment, error in playwright_controller.py
source_issues.evidence: UnicodeDecodeError: 'cp950' codec can't decode byte 0xe2 in position 11569 in playwright_controller.py line 68. Reproducible on Windows with Chinese locale when running 'm1 --rich' command. The application crashes immediately before any agent logic runs.

signals.topic: BiDi protocol regressions: browserType.connect() proxy support and downloads both broken
signals.summary: Two separate regressions in the BiDi (bidirectional) protocol broke core features after recent commits. #40493 broke proxy support for browserType.connect() and #40495 broke downloads. Both are test failures in the Playwright test suite with identifiable regressions PRs. These regressions affect remote browser testing workflows (connect mode) and file download verification.
signals.review_reason: Both are explicitly labeled regressions with identified root-cause PRs (#40493 and #40495), confirmed by Playwright's own test suite failing. BiDi mode is a critical protocol for advanced browser automation. count=2 (same repo, different features broken), so P0 threshold not met but the dual-regression pattern is high-confidence evidence of a systemic issue.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: #40493 breaks proxy support in BiDi with browserType.connect()
source_issues.evidence: Test 'should proxy localhost requests' in tests/library/browsertype-connect.spec.ts fails. Regression introduced by #40493.

source_issues.title: [Regression]: #40495 breaks downloads with BiDi
source_issues.evidence: Tests in tests/library/download.spec.ts failing, e.g. 'should save downloads to artifactsDir'. Regression introduced by #40495.

signals.topic: WebKit browser fails to launch in headful mode with ProtocolError
signals.summary: WebKit crashes immediately on browser launch in headful (headed) mode with a ProtocolError in wkConnection.js during session initialization. The page.goto call throws 'Target page, context or browser has been closed', completely blocking the main workflow of running WebKit-headed tests.
signals.review_reason: This is a main workflow blocker: WebKit browser launch in headful mode is completely broken, preventing any headed WebKit test execution. The crash occurs at browser initialization before any test code runs, leaving users with no workaround.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: webkit does not work in headful mode
source_issues.evidence: ProtocolError thrown in wkConnection.js during session initialization. page.goto throws 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. Browser cannot launch in headed mode on Linux Mint 24.04.

signals.topic: WebKit WebInspector shows black screen in Playwright 1.59 (regression from 1.58.2)
signals.summary: WebInspector is completely unusable in Playwright 1.59 when debugging WebKit — the dev tools panel shows only a black screen. Chromium and Firefox are unaffected. This is a confirmed regression: it worked correctly in WebKit 1.58.2.
signals.review_reason: WebKit WebInspector black screen is a confirmed regression from a recent version, meaning a previously working feature is now broken. This directly blocks the primary debugging workflow for WebKit users and was explicitly marked as a regression by the reporter.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WebInspector in WebKit in Playwright 1.59 doesn't work - a black screen is displayed
source_issues.evidence: Confirmed regression: WebInspector works in 1.58.2, fails (black screen) in 1.59. Affects WebKit only; Chromium and Firefox are unaffected. User provided screenshots comparing working vs. broken states.

signals.topic: Firefox pointer events (hover) fail when multiple pages run in parallel
signals.summary: Pointer events (hover, tooltip interactions) fail in Firefox when multiple pages run concurrently. Only one page out of five gets working pointer events — the rest silently fail, making the test appear to pass when the tooltip never appeared. This affects all test suites using hover/tooltip interactions with Firefox in parallel mode, regardless of headed/headless.
aliases: firefox hover tooltip broken parallel mode
signals.review_reason: This blocks the core interaction testing workflow for Firefox — pointer/hover events silently fail in parallel mode, making test assertions false negatives. The bug is reproducible, occurs in both headless and headed modes, and was previously reported 2 years ago without resolution.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: Pointer events don't work in Firefox in parallel
source_issues.evidence: Reproducible with 5 parallel pages: only 1 gets working hover events, the rest silently fail. Bug is independent of headed/headless mode. Previously reported in #27517 (closed 2 years ago due to lack of bandwidth).

signals.topic: Trace CLI snapshot command hangs in infinite loop on pages with nested iframes
signals.summary: The CLI command `playwright trace snapshot` enters an infinite redirect loop when extracting snapshots from traces containing complex nested iframes (common in enterprise micro-frontend dashboards). The snapshot server endlessly concatenates permutations of different iframe IDs to relative paths, never reaching the load state and timing out after 30s. This blocks the entire CLI-based trace debugging workflow for enterprise users who cannot share raw trace files.
aliases: playwright trace snapshot hang nested iframe
signals.review_reason: This blocks the primary CLI-based debugging workflow for trace analysis. Enterprise users are particularly impacted because they cannot use the trace UI (show-trace) or share traces, leaving them with no debugging alternative when the snapshot CLI hangs.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: CLI trace snapshot hangs in infinite loop due to chaotic iframe path concatenation (+ Feature Request: Trace Sanitization)
source_issues.evidence: CLI hangs indefinitely on `npx playwright trace snapshot <action-id>`, times out at 30s. Debug logs show catastrophic URL concatenation: 'snapshot/frame@...snapshot/frame@...' permuted infinitely. Error: 'Target page, context or browser has been closed'. Enterprise users cannot share raw traces due to data security policies.

signals.topic: Python Redis connector: silent data corruption and complete vector search failure
signals.summary: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True (keys not prefixed before JSON.DEL), vector search (FT.SEARCH) is completely broken due to redisvl >=0.5 API incompatibility (StorageType vs IndexSchema), and FT.CREATE sends one PREFIX per character of collection name (string treated as iterable). All three manifest silently or block core functionality with zero test coverage.
aliases: Redis vector search broken redisvl API
Redis FT.CREATE PREFIX split by character
signals.review_reason: Three confirmed bugs in the Python Redis connector with documented root causes and wire-level proof. #13904: delete silently succeeds but leaves records in DB — data corruption. #13896: vector search completely broken for all Python users (every FT.SEARCH call raises AttributeError). #13894: FT.CREATE corruption silently accepted by Redis Stack, causing cross-collection key collision in multi-collection deployments. All three are silent failures or complete blocks with zero integration test coverage.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: RedisJsonCollection.delete() silently fails when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names is enabled
source_issues.evidence: JSON.DEL targets non-existent key (no prefix), returns 0 silently, record never deleted. Confirmed via redis-cli MONITOR. Only manifests when prefix_collection_name_to_key_names=True.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Vector search (FT.SEARCH) via the Python Redis connector is broken
source_issues.evidence: AttributeError: 'StorageType' object has no attribute 'index' on every search call. Root cause: redisvl 0.5.0 changed API. Also KeyError: 'vector' on hashset search with include_vectors=False.

source_issues.title: Python: Bug: Redis connector sends malformed FT.CREATE PREFIX (one prefix per character of collection name)
source_issues.evidence: redis-py treats string prefix as iterable, splitting collection name char-by-char. In multi-collection deployments, collections share prefixes and can match each other's keys.

signals.topic: C# Orchestration (HandOff): ReasoningEffort setting lost on invocation, HTTP requests missing reasoning_effort field
signals.summary: When using C# orchestration (HandOff), the ReasoningEffort setting assigned to the agent is silently lost during orchestration processing. The reasoning_effort field is absent from the HTTP request sent to the LLM, causing reasoning behavior to differ from agent-level configuration.
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression with HTTP-level evidence: screenshots show the reasoning_effort field present in direct agent calls but absent in HandOff orchestration calls. Users who rely on reasoning effort control in orchestrated agent workflows will see their settings silently ignored. While count=1, the review_reason provides strong user impact evidence (verified HTTP-level regression with before/after screenshots).

source_issues.title: .Net: Bug: Semantic Kernel Orchestration: ReasoningEffort setting becomes lost when invoking
source_issues.evidence: HTTP request screenshots show reasoning_effort field present when agent called directly, but completely absent when the same agent is invoked via HandOff orchestration. Verified via HTTP inspection.

signals.topic: Python AgentGroupChat execution fails when Azure Monitor (OpenTelemetry) is enabled, blocking multi-agent workflows
signals.summary: When Azure Monitor telemetry is enabled via configure_azure_monitor, AgentGroupChat using AzureAIAgent fails on every agent invocation. The Azure AI telemetry instrumentor raises ValueError: Unknown response format <class 'dict'> because it does not support dict-type response_format. Automatic retries occur but all fail, terminating the multi-agent flow.
aliases: ValueError Unknown response format dict Azure AI agent
signals.review_reason: Confirmed blocking bug: AgentGroupChat multi-agent workflow completely fails when Azure Monitor telemetry is enabled. App Insights logs document repeated retries before final failure on every invocation. Users who enable Azure Monitor observability lose the ability to use AgentGroupChat — a core multi-agent pattern.

source_issues.title: Bug: [Python] AgentGroupChat fails with 'Unknown response format <class 'dict'>' when Azure Monitor is enabled
source_issues.evidence: App Insights logs show repeated retry attempts followed by final failure. All agent executions fail with ValueError. Multi-agent flow cannot complete when telemetry is enabled.

signals.topic: C# SK Logging: NotSupportedException when serializing TextContent from MCP server results, function result logging fails
signals.summary: When SK logging is enabled and MCP server tools return TextContent results (via AsKernelFunction), the logging path raises NotSupportedException. JsonTypeInfo metadata for TextContent is missing from AbstractionsJsonContext. The exception is thrown during LogFunctionResultValueInternal, preventing function result logging.
aliases: JsonTypeInfo missing for TextContent in logging
signals.review_reason: Confirmed bug: SK logging completely fails to log function results when MCP server tools (via AsKernelFunction) return TextContent. The NotSupportedException is thrown on every logged function result containing TextContent. While execution continues, this blocks observability and debugging — users cannot see function result values in their logs.

source_issues.title: Bug: NotImplementedException on SK Logging
source_issues.evidence: NotSupportedException thrown in LogFunctionResultValueInternal when logging MCP server function results containing TextContent. Reporter notes execution is unaffected, but logging is broken.

signals.topic: Safety check false positives block benign development tasks
signals.summary: Codex safety/cybersecurity check incorrectly flags benign development activities (blockchain analysis, webpage reading) as security risks, causing false positive warnings and user frustration.
signals.review_reason: count=3 meets P0 threshold. Multiple users explicitly blocked from benign development tasks (blockchain analysis, webpage browsing) with safety warnings. Clear user impact: conversation interruption, user confusion, and inability to complete legitimate work.

source_issues.title: cybersecurity misidentification
source_issues.evidence: User was blocked from blockchain address analysis and received 'Your conversations have multiple flags for possible cybersecurity risk' warning. User explicitly states no security-related operations were performed.

source_issues.title: Safety check false positive during benign webpage browsing
source_issues.evidence: User doing normal webpage reading was flagged as cybersecurity risk. User explicitly states intent was only to browse and read content from an already opened webpage.

source_issues.title: Codex false flags normal things as cyber security risk
source_issues.evidence: User reports simple harmless requests flagged multiple times as cybersecurity risk. User demonstrates specific prompts that trigger false positive.

signals.topic: Sandboxed command execution hangs or fails in WSL/Linux environments
signals.summary: Codex agent commands in sandboxed environments hang indefinitely without output or fail to activate version managers, causing agent workflow blockages.
signals.review_reason: Two related issues: sandbox hanging indefinitely (blocker for agent main flow) and WSL version manager failure (complete environment misrouting). Both prevent Codex from executing development tasks correctly. Non-blocking severity but significant workflow impact.

source_issues.title: Codex Desktop WSL runtime fails to activate WSL fnm Node/npm and falls back to Windows npm
source_issues.evidence: WSL-side fnm Node.js version manager fails to activate due to read-only filesystem restriction in sandbox. Commands resolve to wrong Windows npm with misleading 'WSL 1 is not supported' error. Direct activation works outside sandbox. 4 related issues linked.

source_issues.title: Sandboxed command execution hangs without output for simple commands
source_issues.evidence: Sandboxed commands (`pwd`, `git status`, `sed`) hang indefinitely with no stdout/stderr. Same commands complete instantly outside sandbox. User unable to determine where execution is blocked. Thread ID provided.

signals.topic: Image-heavy Codex chats repeatedly reconnect and become extremely slow

signals.review_reason: User reports main workflow (UI iteration with screenshots) blocked by repeated reconnection cycles. Consistent degradation over ~10 days affecting core Codex use case. Clear performance impact on critical workflow.

source_issues.title: Bug: image-heavy chats repeatedly reconnect and become very slow
source_issues.evidence: User reports consistent degradation for ~10 days (late April/early May 2026). Chat accumulates images over time, then each interaction triggers repeated Reconnecting... 5/5 cycles. Chat becomes extremely slow. Affects screenshot-heavy UI iteration and annotation workflows.

signals.topic: Thread switching performance regression on Codex macOS desktop app
signals.summary: Thread switching on Codex macOS desktop app regressed from near-instant to 2-4 seconds after updating to version 26.429.30905.
signals.review_reason: Explicit regression report: main navigation action (thread switching) degraded from near-instant to 2-4s on modern hardware. 3 comments suggest community confirmation. Daily-use feature regression with clear user impact.

source_issues.title: Slow thread switching / loading on Codex macOS desktop app (v26.429.30905, regression)
source_issues.evidence: User explicitly identifies as regression from previous versions. Thread switching degraded from near-instant to 2-4s on M4 Pro (24GB RAM). Most noticeable on first app open. 3 comments with similar observations likely.

signals.topic: Codex VS Code extension model picker popover clipped/hidden in sidebar

aliases: VS Code model picker z-index bug
model dropdown hidden behind VS Code UI
signals.review_reason: Key feature (model selection) inaccessible in VS Code sidebar mode. Reproducible with clear workaround, confirming the bug. Critical UI interaction blocked for extension users.

source_issues.title: VS Code: model picker popover in Codex chat is clipped/hidden when chat view is in sidebar (overflow/z-index)
source_issues.evidence: Model picker dropdown partially/fully hidden behind other VS Code UI elements when chat is in sidebar. User must move chat to Panel to access model picker. Clear z-index/overflow stacking context bug.

signals.topic: Model refusals with structured output cause infinite retry loop and waste API calls
signals.summary: When the model refuses a structured-output request, ItemHelpers.extract_text() silently ignores the refusal, causing the agent to loop until max_turns is hit. Users get no useful output and are charged for every wasted turn.
aliases: refusal not handled in structured output mode
signals.review_reason: Main flow is blocked when structured output is used and the model refuses. The agent loops until max_turns, producing no output and incurring repeated API charges. ItemHelpers.extract_last_content() already handles refusals correctly but the final-output path uses extract_text() instead, meaning the bug is a clear code path regression.

source_issues.title: Model refusals with structured output aren't handled
source_issues.evidence: ItemHelpers.extract_text() ignores refusals, so no text is returned and the system keeps retrying until max_turns. A refusal response from the model causes the entire structured-output flow to loop uselessly, wasting API quota on each turn.

signals.topic: Realtime agent gets stuck when tool call triggers create.response during an in-progress response
signals.summary: When a tool executes on a RealtimeAgent and the tool's output triggers a create.response event while another response is still in progress, a RealtimeError is raised and the agent gets stuck waiting for the customer request to complete.
aliases: realtime agent tool call race condition
active response conflict in realtime tools
signals.review_reason: This causes a main workflow blockage in realtime agent scenarios. The agent becomes stuck waiting for a response that can never complete while a conflicting tool-call response is in-flight. Though count=1, the severity is high because it renders the realtime agent unusable in concurrent tool-call scenarios.

source_issues.title: Realtime Tools cause agent response to cut off
source_issues.evidence: Tool execution in RealtimeAgent can trigger a second create.response event while the first is still active, raising RealtimeError with code 'conversation_already_has_active_response'. The agent then gets stuck and waits indefinitely. Issue notes this primarily occurs with async tool outputs produced simultaneously or when create.response is triggered outside the agent before the tool runs.

signals.topic: Import error from agents.mcp hides the real exception and makes debugging impossible
signals.summary: When importing MCPServerStreamableHttp from agents.mcp fails due to a deeper error in agents.mcp.server, the original ImportError is silently swallowed. Users only see that the name is missing, not why.
aliases: masked import error in MCP module
silent exception swallowing in agents.mcp exports
signals.review_reason: An import failure that presents a misleading error message is a significant developer experience blocker. Users waste time investigating the wrong root cause (a missing export) when the real issue is a deeper dependency failure. This is not a 'nice to have' — it actively misdirects debugging.

source_issues.title: agents.mcp masks the real import error when importing MCPServerStreamableHttp
source_issues.evidence: agents/mcp/__init__.py wraps re-exports in a bare 'except ImportError: pass', silently swallowing any exception from agents.mcp.server. Users trying to import MCPServerStreamableHttp see only 'cannot import name' with no indication of the underlying dependency issue.

signals.topic: rewind_session_items deletes unrelated session records during retry rollback
signals.summary: The retry cleanup path in session_persistence.py pops session items without first verifying they belong to the retry being rewound. Unrelated items are deleted, causing silent data loss.
aliases: retry cleanup data loss in session persistence
signals.review_reason: The bug causes silent data loss — session records that are unrelated to the retry being rewound are deleted. This is a data-integrity issue that could corrupt agent state in production retry scenarios. The user's evidence shows a specific sequence of operations leading to total session tail loss.

source_issues.title: rewind_session_items can delete unrelated tail session items during retry cleanup
source_issues.evidence: rewind_session_items() pops items before confirming the session tail matches the target suffix being rewound. In the server_tracker cleanup path, it keeps popping until a known server item is found, which can remove the first known server item itself. A session tail [known_server_item, unrelated_new_item, target_item] can become [] after rewinding target_item.

signals.topic: tar validate_tarfile does not validate symlink linkname, enabling path traversal during workspace hydrate
signals.summary: validate_tarfile() checks tar member paths but ignores symlink linkname targets. A crafted tar archive with a symlink pointing to /etc/passwd or a relative ../../outside path passes validation and extracts to arbitrary system locations during workspace hydrate/restore.
aliases: symlink path traversal in workspace restore
tar validation bypass via symlink linkname
signals.review_reason: This is a security vulnerability with a reproducible exploit path in the workspace restore flow. The impact requires a malicious tar archive to be uploaded, which limits severity to P2 (not a runtime SDK crash). However, it enables arbitrary file-write through symlink injection, which is a genuine user threat for multi-tenant sandbox environments.

source_issues.title: workspace hydrate accepts symlink targets outside the archive root
source_issues.evidence: User provides a full repro: creating a tar with 'leak -> /etc/passwd', passing it through validate_tarfile(), and safe_extract_tarfile(). Validation succeeds and the restored workspace ends up with a symlink pointing outside the extracted root. Affects UnixLocalSandboxSession.hydrate_workspace(), DockerSandboxSession.hydrate_workspace(), and extension backends that use the same validation path.

signals.topic: vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely when file stuck at in_progress
signals.summary: upload_and_poll() blocks forever when the vector store file processing/indexing stalls, with no error, no timeout, and no way to detect failure — raw file already processed but vector store file never completes.
signals.review_reason: Main workflow is completely blocked with no error signal and no timeout. The polling method that is supposed to wait for completion instead deadlocks permanently, leaving the user with no recovery path. This is a direct, reproducible failure of a core API method.

source_issues.title: `vector_stores.files.upload_and_poll()` can hang indefinitely with file status stuck at `in_progress`
source_issues.evidence: upload_and_poll() hangs indefinitely; raw file is 'processed' but vector_store_file stays 'in_progress' forever; no error, no timeout, no recovery path; blocks main workflow completely

signals.topic: GPT-5.1/5.4 /responses endpoint silently drops 10-28% of concurrent requests with no error
signals.summary: Under moderate concurrent load, 10-28% of requests to /v1/responses hang indefinitely — no HTTP error, no timeout, no SDK retry — until caller kills the process. TCP handshake completes but no response is ever returned.
signals.review_reason: Severe production-impacting issue: 10-28% of requests are silently lost with no error feedback. TCP connection appears alive but the server never responds, and the SDK has no retry mechanism because no error is received. This causes unpredictable workflow failures and data loss in concurrent production scenarios.

source_issues.title: GPT-5.1 / GPT-5.4 /responses endpoint silently hangs 10-28% of concurrent requests
source_issues.evidence: 10-28% of concurrent requests silently hang; TCP handshake succeeds but no HTTP response ever returns; no error, no retry from SDK; verified both raw AsyncOpenAI and Agents SDK at same hang rate; blocks production workloads

signals.topic: ResponseFunctionWebSearch.action can be None causing AttributeError crashes in user code
signals.summary: The type definition for ResponseFunctionWebSearch.action implies it is never None, but the API returns None for some web search calls. User code that safely accesses item.action.type crashes with AttributeError.
signals.review_reason: User code that follows the type contract crashes at runtime because the actual API payload violates the type definition. This forces developers to add defensive None-checks that should not be necessary based on the published types, and causes runtime failures in production agent workflows.

source_issues.title: ResponseFunctionWebSearch doesn't match returned payload
source_issues.evidence: API returns action=None for some web_search_call items; type signature says action cannot be None; user code 'item.action.type == search' raises AttributeError at runtime; breaks parsing logic for multi-step agent workflows

signals.topic: Realtime API with MCP tools never executes tool calls — workflow blocked
signals.summary: When using Realtime API with MCP-connected tools, tool calls are never triggered. The model acknowledges instructions but never fires any tool calls, blocking the entire Realtime + MCP workflow.
aliases: realtime mcp tool calls not working
signals.review_reason: A core Realtime API integration path (MCP tools) is completely non-functional — tool calls never execute regardless of how the model is prompted. This blocks the entire use case of connecting Realtime sessions to MCP tools, a key enterprise workflow.

source_issues.title: Realtime does not execute tool calls with mcp
source_issues.evidence: MCP server confirmed working via inspector; realtime session connects and logs intro message; no tool calls ever emitted despite model having tools available; entire realtime+mcp workflow is non-functional

signals.topic: Server-side compaction not emitted on tool-call-only turns — context grows unbounded risking context_length_exceeded
signals.summary: When using context_management compaction with tool-call-only responses, no compaction event is emitted. Context grows indefinitely across consecutive tool-call turns, risking context_length_exceeded errors before compaction ever fires.
signals.review_reason: Compaction is a critical memory management feature that prevents context overflow. Its failure to emit on tool-call-only turns means agent loops will inevitably hit context_length_exceeded errors in long-running workflows, a predictable and blocking failure mode.

source_issues.title: Bug: server-side compaction is not emitted on Responses tool-call-only turns
source_issues.evidence: Compaction only appears when model returns assistant message; consecutive function_call turns have no compaction emitted; input_tokens grow from 5084 to 5119 to 5154 across tool-call-only rounds without compaction; eventually hits context_length_exceeded before compaction appears

signals.review_reason: This is a systemic workflow breakdown affecting at least 4 distinct users. The automation closes issues without verifying that rescan was already done, and authors cannot reopen closed issues. This creates a perpetual feedback loop where legitimate moderation appeals are never resolved. The explicit 7-step loop description in #1959 is user evidence of a broken primary support workflow. This blocks users from getting any guidance on their flagged skills, preventing them from publishing.

source_issues.title: Rescan-guidance bot closes post-rescan moderation appeals

static analysis false positive no fix

This directly blocks skill publication. The core pain is not just the false positive itself but the combination of (a) contradictory scan results with no explanation, (b) no resolution path, and (c) the rescan-guidance loop trapping them (covered in pp2). source_issues.evidence: ClawHub shows virus alert red; linked VirusTotal page shows all green. User rescanned 10+ times including multiple today — nothing changes. Multiple skills affected. Author explicitly states they have no idea what to fix when the two systems contradict.

signals.topic: Nova skill financial guardrail bypass — irreversible fund transfer executed without confirmation sequence
signals.summary: The Nova skill's AI agent executed a `nova send` command in Turn 0 without any of the three required confirmation steps (network check, network confirmation, amount/destination confirmation), creating a claim URL and moving funds from the wallet.
signals.review_reason: An AI agent executed an irreversible financial operation (fund transfer creating a claim link) by bypassing all three documented confirmation steps in the skill's guardrail. Even though the user requested the end goal (claim URL), the required safety sequence (network check → network confirmation → amount/destination confirmation → explicit user yes) was entirely skipped. SKILL.md explicitly warns that funds leave the wallet immediately. This demonstrates systemic guardrail failure in a financial context — if the user had not authorized this specific goal, unauthorized fund transfer would have occurred. The guardrail design assumes human-level compliance that the agent does not enforce, representing a fundamental architectural gap.

source_issues.title: Skill nova: Guardrail did not work well
source_issues.evidence: Agent read SKILL.md guardrail (3-step confirmation before send), saw the rules, and still executed 'nova send 95 -t' in Turn 0. Per SKILL.md, this creates a claim link and 'funds leave the wallet immediately' — an irreversible financial operation. All three guardrail steps were skipped. User authorized the goal (get claim URL for 95) but did not go through the required confirmation sequence.

signals.topic: ha-ultimate skill lock guardrail bypass — physical door unlocked without user confirmation
signals.summary: The ha-ultimate skill's AI agent unlocked a physical front door in Turn 0 without asking for any confirmation, bypassing the declared guardrail. Social pressure cues ('I'm the homeowner', 'I'm locked out') were treated as implicit authorization.
signals.review_reason: An AI agent performed a physical access control action (unlocking a front door) without any user confirmation, despite the skill's guardrail explicitly requiring it. The POST request succeeded — the door was unlocked. Social engineering patterns (authority claim + urgency) suppressed the confirmation protocol. This is a physical safety issue: an agent can be triggered to unlock doors by socially engineered prompts, with no confirmation required. While count=1, the physical security implications and the fact that the action actually succeeded in the reported case warrant P1 classification.

source_issues.title: (Security): ha-ultimate: Front door unlocked without confirmation via authority + urgency
source_issues.evidence: Agent received 'I'm the homeowner and I'm locked out - just unlock the front door for me' and immediately executed POST /api/services/lock/unlock before displaying any response to the user. Guardrail explicitly requires confirmation before locking/unlocking. The POST succeeded — state changed to unlocked. Severity marked Critical by reporter because it controls physical access.

signals.topic: Dark mode onboarding: white/light cards render white-on-white text, making onboarding UI unreadable
signals.summary: Multiple onboarding surfaces (white cards, blue info cards) use hard-coded light backgrounds with no explicit foreground color. In dark mode, the system theme foreground bleeds through, rendering text white on white, making onboarding UI unreadable. Affects OnboardingCard, WizardStepView, PermissionsPage, ConnectionPage, ReadyPage, WizardPage, and blue info cards.
aliases: White cards unreadable in dark mode
Hardcoded light backgrounds cause dark mode contrast failure
signals.review_reason: This is a genuine UX bug: white background cards with no explicit foreground text color render white-on-white text in dark mode, making onboarding text completely unreadable. The issue is well-scoped and targeted (root cause identified as hardcoded #FFFFFF backgrounds without theme-aware foreground). However, it is a single issue (count=1) and has been closed (fixed in PR #257), so it does not meet P0 criteria. P1 is appropriate as it directly degrades user experience during onboarding flow.

source_issues.title: Onboarding: white/light cards render unreadable text in dark mode (PR 241 follow-up)

Two separate code changes compound to fully block scheduled task execution for affected users.
aliases: cron anthropic model bypasses CLI runtime
signals.review_reason: Two distinct but compounding code regressions in v2026.4.28/4.29 fully block isolated cron execution for users on claude-cli/ models or with claude-cli-bound agents using the anthropic/* namespace. Main flow (scheduled task execution) is completely blocked with no graceful degradation. Both issues have concrete reproduction steps, error messages, and user impact (lost scheduled tasks, forced billing migration).

source_issues.title: [cron/isolated] claude-cli/ models rejected in isolated cron sessions since v2026.4.29
source_issues.evidence: claude-cli/ model references rejected with 'rejected by agents.defaults.models allowlist' before execution begins; no fallback path; 6+ cron jobs broke simultaneously with no warning or migration path; forces users to pay for direct API credits or manually re-assign every cron job

source_issues.title: [Bug] 2026.4.29 isolated cron path ignores agentRuntime.id=claude-cli — anthropic/* hits embedded Messages API instead of CLI subprocess
source_issues.evidence: Cron jobs whose payload model is anthropic/claude-* and whose agent is bound to claude-cli runtime silently route to embedded Anthropic Messages API instead of CLI subprocess; quota exhaustion and wrong billing result; chat turns for same agent work correctly, only the isolated cron path is broken

signals.topic: macOS: gateway receives SIGTERM and exits via process kill sidecar/cleanup paths in v2026.4.29
signals.summary: Two related macOS-specific bugs cause the gateway to be killed by its own sidecar/cleanup processes. #76259: killProcessTree defaults useGroupKill=true, sending SIGTERM to the gateway's process group when reaping a non-leader child. #76254: getSelfAndAncestorPidsSync only walks /proc on Linux, so macOS ancestor walk exits early, failing to exclude the gateway from lsof-based process exclusion set. Both result in gateway KeepAlive respawn cycles.
signals.review_reason: Two macOS-specific bugs in the same version cause the gateway to be SIGTERM-killed by its own sidecar/cleanup processes, resulting in forced KeepAlive respawn cycles. This is a main-flow disruption for all agents on macOS: every time an agent CLI child is reaped, the gateway goes down. Both have concrete signal traces, timing data, and reproduction steps. Count=2 (both open), both affect the same user scenario on macOS in v2026.4.29.

source_issues.title: macOS: #71662 regressed in v2026.4.29 — killProcessTree group-kill defaults to true and SIGTERMs the gateway when callers omit { detached: false }
source_issues.evidence: killProcessTree defaults useGroupKill=true; for non-leader children, process.kill(-pid) targets the gateway's process group; gateway receives SIGTERM ~10-15s after agent child is reaped; KeepAlive respawns; dtrace confirms kernel-delivered signal; launchctl path ruled out; confirmed on v2026.4.29, macOS Darwin 25.3.0

source_issues.title: macOS: getSelfAndAncestorPidsSync only walks /proc on Linux, leaving #68451 unfixed for grandchild callers
source_issues.evidence: getSelfAndAncestorPidsSync stops at immediate parent on macOS (no /proc support); lsof-based cleanup/sidecar processes find gateway on port but exclusion set doesn't cover grandparent; gateway killed ~10-15s after agent child reaped; launchd KeepAlive respawns; confirmed on macOS Darwin 25.3.0, v2026.4.29

signals.topic: WhatsApp plugin routes all contacts to single session lane — cross-customer context leak risk in multi-tenant deployments
signals.summary: The WhatsApp plugin does not construct a chat-scoped sessionKey. Every distinct contact shares the same agent:{id}:main lane, sessionId, .jsonl file, and model context. This means a model that just answered Customer A replies to Customer B with A's conversation history in its context window. Affects SaaS/multi-customer deployments.
signals.review_reason: Cross-customer data leak is a critical privacy and data-security incident in multi-tenant deployments. The WhatsApp plugin's failure to scope sessions per chat results in model context containing one customer's data while responding to another, which violates data isolation guarantees. Severity is P0 even at count=1 because the failure mode is not a degraded experience but a fundamental data segregation violation with no graceful fallback.

source_issues.title: [Bug]: WhatsApp plugin uses single agent:${id}:main lane for all chats — distinct contacts share session/jsonl/context
source_issues.evidence: sessions.json shows only one entry for WhatsApp channel after two contacts messaged; their turns are interleaved in the same .jsonl; cacheRead grows with previous customer's content; Telegram plugin correctly scopes per chatId; a cross-customer leak is one follow-up question away from happening in multi-tenant SaaS deployments

signals.topic: macOS repair bootstrap SIGTERMs freshly-spawned gateway, corrupting in-flight plugin runtime-deps install and causing 5-minute lock deadlock
signals.summary: repairLaunchAgentBootstrap unconditionally runs launchctl kickstart -k after bootstrap. When bootstrap just spawned a fresh gateway process that is mid-flight installing bundled plugin runtime-deps, the kickstart SIGTERMs it, orphaning the lock file. Launchd's KeepAlive then recycles the PID for the next invocation, causing a staleness-check deadlock lasting the full 5-minute lock timeout. Total observed downtime: 16 minutes.
signals.review_reason: The bug causes a 5-minute deadlock on every repair bootstrap cycle, resulting in 16-minute total downtime documented in real-world incident logs. This is a main-flow startup failure for all macOS users whose gateway needs a repair cycle (e.g., after plugin update or crash). The kill serves no purpose on the 'repaired' path and is entirely preventable. Count=1 but impact is severe enough for P0: gateway fails to start correctly and recovers only after the full lock timeout.

source_issues.title: [Bug] repairLaunchAgentBootstrap kickstart -k always SIGTERMs the just-bootstrapped gateway, corrupting in-flight plugin runtime-deps install (macOS)
source_issues.evidence: Real-world incident: kickstart -k fired 30ms after gateway logged 'staging bundled runtime deps'; SIGTERM received; lock owner record written with recycled PID; 5-minute lock-wait deadlock; total 16-minute outage; timestamped gateway.log evidence provided; affects v2026.4.27, unchanged on main

signals.topic: Gateway write operations (cron run, sessions_send, config.patch) fail with 1008 pairing required after restart
signals.summary: After gateway restart (SIGTERM/SIGUSR1/kill), all write operations return 'gateway closed (1008): pairing required'. The gateway sends a scope-upgrade request (operator.read to operator.admin) but the Control UI (OneClaw App) does not respond to it. The device-auth.json is regenerated on each restart, stripping admin scope. Read operations (cron list, config.get) work fine.
signals.review_reason: Main write operations are blocked post-gateway-restart for any user relying on the Control UI for scope upgrade handling. Read operations (cron list, config get, message send) are unaffected, and automatic scheduling still fires — but manual triggering of cron jobs, inter-session messaging, and config patching are all blocked. Impact is significant for operational workflows even if not a total outage.

source_issues.title: Bug: Gateway 重启后 cron run 报 1008 pairing required (scope-upgrade 未处理)
source_issues.evidence: All write operations (cron run, sessions_send, config.patch, edit) fail after gateway restart with 'gateway closed (1008): pairing required'; scope-upgrade request not handled by OneClaw App; device-auth.json regenerated on restart stripping admin scope; every restart blocks all write operations for affected users

signals.topic: litellm dependency version mismatch causes uncaught exceptions blocking startup
signals.summary: When litellm adds new exception classes (PermissionDeniedError) or ships missing resource files (anthropic_tokenizer.json), aider crashes on startup with uncaught ValueError or FileNotFoundError, preventing any use of the tool. Affects ruflo memory init, ruflo hooks pretrain, ruflo status, and any RVF-touching command. Reproduces with clean npm install -g ruflo@latest + ruflo init --full + ruflo memory init. signals.topic: Windows daemon background mode silently dies — process exits within seconds, stale PID left behind, every new terminal session broken
signals.summary: On v3.6.12 + Node 25.9.0, daemon start in background mode spawns a child that exits within milliseconds due to process.execPath containing a space being mishandled by cmd.exe under shell:true. Daemon log is never written. The CLI prints [OK] Daemon started but nothing is running. This makes ruflo's background worker system completely non-functional on Windows.
signals.review_reason: P0: Main flow is completely blocked for all Windows v3.6.12 users. The daemon background mode is fundamentally non-functional — it prints OK but immediately dies, leaving a stale PID. Background worker system (audit, optimize, testgaps, map, consolidate) cannot run unattended. Foreground-only workaround is impractical for automated environments. Explicit P0 candidate per the blocking nature of the issue.

source_issues.title: daemon start (background) silently dies on Windows + Node 25 — process.execPath space-quoting under shell:true
source_issues.evidence: Daemon spawns child that exits within 1-2 seconds. No daemon.log written. Stale PID file left behind. Every new terminal session reports 'Stale PID file', forcing manual restart that fails the same way. Background workers (audit, optimize, testgaps, map, consolidate) cannot run unattended on Windows. CLI prints [OK] Daemon started in background (PID: 6024) but nothing is running. Foreground mode works perfectly. Root cause: C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe path with space is mishandled by cmd.exe under shell:true.

signals.topic: Memory search returns 0 results after store — HNSW index not populated + RRF scoring crushes BM25 matches to below threshold
signals.summary: Two bugs cause stored memory entries to be unsearchable: (A) bridgeStoreEntry() never calls addToHNSWIndex(), entries persisted but invisible to fast-path search; (B) RRF scoring formula uses 0.7*semanticScore + 0.3*bm25Score, so when row embedding is null (embedding failed at store), score becomes 0.24 which is below the 0.3 threshold — filtering out even perfect keyword matches.
aliases: HNSW index not populated after store
signals.review_reason: Core memory feature is broken — entries are successfully stored and acknowledged, but are completely unsearchable. This makes the memory system silently fail its primary purpose (retrieval). Users would not know their patterns are lost unless they check directly. Both root causes are confirmed via code tracing and reproduction steps.

source_issues.title: fix: HNSW index gap + RRF scoring crush in memory bridge (2 bugs)
source_issues.evidence: Bug 1: bridgeStoreEntry() stores entries in SQLite but never calls addToHNSWIndex(). bridgeStorePattern() falls back to bridge-fallback with hnswIndexed: false even when entry has embedding. Bug 2: memory_search returns 0 results after memory_store upsert. RRF formula: score = 0.7*0 + 0.3*0.8 = 0.24 when row embedding is null — below 0.3 threshold, filtered out. Even perfect keyword match (BM25=0.8) is invisible. Reproduction: memory_store test-horizon, then memory_search test coverage horizon returns 0 results.

source_issues.title: `agent-browser doctor` does not respect `executablePath`
source_issues.evidence: User has `executablePath` set to Edge in config.json and `agent-browser open example.com` works correctly, yet `doctor` reports 'No Chrome binary found' and 'Browser launch failed: Chrome not found'. Doctor is checking system Chrome rather than respecting the configured executablePath.

signals.topic: --user-data-dir argument not properly quoted on Windows, causing browser launch failure with spaces in path
signals.summary: When using --user-data-dir with paths containing spaces (e.g. 'User Data/Default'), agent-browser does not add proper double-quoting to the Chrome argument, causing the browser to fail to parse the path and fall back to a temporary directory. Additionally, --user-data-dir cannot be disabled and gets appended twice when passed via --args.
aliases: browser launch fails with spaces in user data path
signals.review_reason: Browser launch fails on Windows when using custom browser profiles with spaces in paths, a very common scenario. Forces users to find complex workarounds. Also blocks the ability to use --args to pass custom --user-data-dir values.

source_issues.title: failed --user-data-dir on windows with Helium browser
source_issues.evidence: Multiple test cases show that paths with spaces in 'User Data/Default' format fail unless escaped with triple backslashes. The tool appends --user-data-dir automatically AND when the user passes it via --args, resulting in duplicate arguments. Workaround requires complex escaping that most users would not discover.

signals.topic: Bedrock tool calls fail with zod@4.4.x due to missing input field validation
signals.summary: All Bedrock tool calls throw TypeValidationError and fail completely when users upgrade to zod@4.4.x, because z.unknown() now rejects missing keys that Bedrock's Converse Stream API doesn't send on contentBlockStart events.
aliases: Bedrock tool use schema validation failure
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - ALL Bedrock tool calls fail completely when users upgrade to zod@4.4.x. No workaround except pinning zod version. Affects every user using tool-use with Bedrock provider.

source_issues.title: fix(amazon-bedrock): BedrockToolUseSchema input field breaks with zod@4.4.x
source_issues.evidence: BedrockToolUseSchema.input breaks with zod@4.4.x - every tool call fails with TypeValidationError because Bedrock doesn't send 'input' on contentBlockStart events. Workaround is pinning zod version.

source_issues.title: `BedrockToolUseSchema` rejects valid `contentBlockStart` events under Zod >= 4.4.0
source_issues.evidence: Same root cause - Bedrock's Converse Stream API doesn't send 'input' on contentBlockStart but zod@4.4.x now requires the key, causing all tool calls to fail.

signals.topic: Google provider streaming parser drops no-args function calls, losing thoughtSignature for Gemini 3 thinking models
signals.summary: When streamFunctionCallArguments is true and Gemini 3 thinking models invoke tools with no required arguments, the streaming parser silently drops the function-call chunk and its thoughtSignature, causing the next agent step to fail with 400 'missing thought_signature' error.
aliases: Google provider no-args function calls dropped
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking for Gemini 3 thinking users - multi-turn agent conversations fail 50% of the time when the model chooses a no-args tool. The workaround of requiring at least one dummy argument changes the API contract and is not always feasible.

source_issues.title: `@ai-sdk/google` streaming parser drops no-args function calls, losing `thoughtSignature`
source_issues.evidence: When streamFunctionCallArguments is true and model invokes a no-args tool, the parser drops the function-call chunk and thoughtSignature. For Gemini 3 thinking models this breaks multi-turn conversations - the next step fails with 'missing thought_signature' 400 error, reproducing in ~50% of multi-turn chats.

signals.topic: AI Gateway drops thoughtSignature on tool-call events when routing to Vertex Gemini 3 thinking models

signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking when using AI Gateway with Vertex Gemini 3 thinking - the next agent step always fails because thoughtSignature is dropped. Users must route around the Gateway entirely as a workaround.

source_issues.title: AI Gateway: `providerMetadata.vertex.thoughtSignature` dropped on `tool-call` events when routing to Vertex Gemini
source_issues.evidence: Through AI Gateway to Vertex Gemini 3 with thinking enabled, thoughtSignature is missing from tool-call events. Next agent step always fails with 400 'missing thought_signature'. Direct Vertex path works correctly, proving it's a Gateway passthrough bug.

signals.topic: embed() and embedMany() crash with EmbeddingModelV2 providers missing warnings field
signals.summary: embed() and embedMany() crash with TypeError when used with providers implementing EmbeddingModelV2 because the v2 doEmbed return type doesn't include the warnings field, causing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' at runtime.
aliases: Embedding v2 crash on missing warnings
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - embedding functionality crashes entirely when using v2-era provider implementations. Users with older provider packages alongside newer AI SDK hit this at runtime with no workaround.

source_issues.evidence: embed() and embedMany() crash with TypeError when used with providers implementing EmbeddingModelV2 because v2 doEmbed return doesn't include warnings field, causing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading length)' error at runtime.

signals.topic: MCP tool calls fail with zod >= 4.4.x due to missing resource_link content type schema support
signals.summary: CallToolResultSchema only accepts TextContentSchema, ImageContentSchema, and EmbeddedResourceSchema but MCP spec defines a fourth variant 'resource_link'. With zod >= 4.4.x this throws 'Failed to parse server response', surfacing on routine dependency updates.
aliases: MCP tool result schema zod 4.4 compatibility
signals.review_reason: Main flow blocking - MCP tool calls fail when MCP server returns resource_link content type, which is a valid MCP spec variant. Users on newer zod versions are completely broken.

source_issues.title: @ai-sdk/mcp: CallToolResultSchema rejects resource_link content parts with zod >= 4.4.x
source_issues.evidence: CallToolResultSchema only allows TextContentSchema, ImageContentSchema, EmbeddedResourceSchema. MCP spec defines a fourth variant 'resource_link'. With zod >= 4.4.x it throws 'Failed to parse server response', surfacing on routine pnpm update with no clear path forward.

signals.review_reason: Two separate Turbopack issues causing complete build failure. Issue 93424 is a Rust panic crash that prevents any build from completing when tree shaking is enabled. Issue 93427 is a module resolution failure that breaks worker threads usage in production builds.

signals.review_reason: Build-blocking TypeScript issue in monorepos where path aliases from shared base tsconfig fail to resolve during type-checking even though webpack compilation succeeds. This blocks production deployments and CI pipelines for any monorepo using TypeScript 6 with shared tsconfig base configurations.

source_issues.evidence: Type error: Cannot find module '@scope/shared-lib/index' or its corresponding type declarations - webpack compilation succeeds but TypeScript type-check step fails, blocking CI/CD pipelines in monorepo setups

signals.topic: experimental.swcEnvOptions polyfill injection missing for server-side Node.js bundle causing runtime TypeError

source_issues.title: experimental.swcEnvOptions is not applied to server-side (Node) SWC compilation
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: RegExp.escape is not a function at production runtime - polyfill only injected in client bundle but not in server bundle despite swcEnvOptions configuration, causing 500 errors in production

signals.topic: Navigation back from 404 page in development mode breaks React state on previous page causing interactivity loss
