Affects all developers using Next.js 16.2.x in development - every 404 visit followed by back navigation breaks the app.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16.2.4 - Bug When Navigating Back from 404 in Development
source_issues.evidence: After navigating to 404 page and pressing browser back button, React state is lost on the previous page - counter stops working, buttons unresponsive, static HTML only. Manual refresh fixes it. Does NOT occur in production.

signals.topic: Latest SDK version not published to npm, blocking installation and upgrades
signals.summary: The latest published npm SDK version (1.19.41) is not available in the npm registry, preventing users from installing or upgrading to the newest release via standard package managers.

source_issues.title: Latest npm sdk version not published
source_issues.evidence: User reports version 1.19.41 is not published to npm, with reference to failed CI build (actions/runs/25059772130). Zero comments suggest unaddressed/unresolved.

signals.topic: getProjects API response fails Zod schema validation, causing runtime errors
signals.summary: Calling getProjects returns API responses that do not match the SDK's Zod schema: fields like 'alias' are undefined where arrays are expected, and the 'security' object structure is inconsistent across projects, resulting in ZodError thrown at runtime.
signals.review_reason: getProjects is a core SDK API call. When its response fails Zod validation, the entire call throws an unhandled exception, blocking the primary workflow of retrieving project data. This is a runtime error introduced by a breaking change in the SDK upgrade path, affecting any user calling getProjects in production.

source_issues.title: `getProjects` response validation error
source_issues.evidence: User reports ZodError on every project returned by getProjects after upgrading SDK from 1.18.7 to 1.18.9. The API returns 'alias' as undefined (expected array) and 'security' as inconsistent object shapes. Full ZodError output provided with specific field paths.

signals.topic: turbo prune --docker generates invalid pruned workspaces for package managers (Bun/pnpm)
signals.summary: turbo prune --docker produces invalid pruned workspaces that cause Docker build failures: Bun lockfile is invalid for `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, pnpm lockfile over-matches .gitignore entries, and pnpm missing bin stubs prevents .bin shim creation. All three block the Docker mono-to-micro repo workflow.
aliases: prune docker pnpm bin stubs missing
signals.review_reason: Three distinct bugs in `turbo prune --docker` each block the critical Docker mono-repo deployment workflow. Issue #12653 causes Docker builds to fail outright with bun. Issue #12659 causes wrong file exclusion in pnpm prune. Issue #12610 causes pnpm .bin shims to not be created. All are reproducible with public repos, all are labelled 'kind: bug', and all represent a mainflow failure (Docker CI/CD pipeline broken). Count=3 meets P0 threshold.

source_issues.title: `turbo prune --docker` generates invalid Bun lockfile; `bun install --frozen-lockfile` fails in pruned Docker stage
source_issues.evidence: Docker build fails at `bun install --frozen-lockfile` after `turbo prune --docker`. Error: lockfile had changes, but lockfile is frozen. Verified with public repro and oven/bun:1.3.13-alpine.

source_issues.title: `turbo prune` is overmatching .gitignore entries
source_issues.evidence: Explicit .gitignore rules like `/apps/app-a/coverage` incorrectly exclude deeply nested files (e.g., apps/app-a/src/api/coverage/test.js). Setting --use-gitignore=false works around it. Root cause in crates/turborepo-fs/src/lib.rs.

source_issues.title: prune --docker: create stub source files for bin entries
source_issues.evidence: Pruned workspace only contains package.json, so pnpm refuses to create .bin shims for internal tools. Build scripts that need those tools fail. Public Docker repro confirms the failure.

signals.topic: turbo 2.9.7 high-CPU child processes spawned for persistent tasks under tmux
signals.summary: Upgrading to turbo 2.9.7 causes excessive child turbo processes (one per persistent task) to consume full CPU cores when running persistent tasks inside tmux sessions, making machines hot/noisy while watch tasks are idle. Downgrading to 2.9.6 immediately resolves it.
aliases: high CPU child processes under tmux
signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression in 2.9.7 vs 2.9.6: persistent watch tasks cause multiple extra high-CPU child turbo processes. Each process consumes ~full CPU core for minutes, making machines hot and noisy. Root cause bisected to a 2.9.7 change. This is a mainflow performance regression affecting all tmux/tmux-like environments running persistent tasks.

source_issues.title: Turbo 2.9.7 spawns high-CPU child turbo processes for persistent tasks under tmux
source_issues.evidence: Regression in 2.9.7 confirmed: each persistent task spawns an extra high-CPU child turbo process consuming ~90-100% CPU. Reproduced in tmux with Bun 1.3.13. Downgrade to 2.9.6 fixes immediately.

signals.topic: pnpm 11 lockfile flat-string patchedDependencies format causes turbo parse warnings and degraded cache
signals.summary: Turbo fails to parse pnpm 11's new flat-string format for patchedDependencies, emitting a warning on every turbo run and falling back to file-content hashing instead of lockfile-aware cache invalidation.
signals.review_reason: Non-fatal but noisy: every turbo run in a pnpm 11 monorepo with patches emits a warning and degrades cache from lockfile-aware to file-content hashing. This is not a complete failure but causes CI noise and suboptimal caching performance across all affected pnpm 11 users.

source_issues.title: Turbo cannot parse pnpm 11 lockfiles with new flat-string `patchedDependencies` format
source_issues.evidence: pnpm 11 changed patchedDependencies from {path, hash} struct to flat hash string. turbo's Rust PatchFile struct fails to deserialize. Warning emitted on every run. Cache degrades from lockfile-aware to file-content hashing. Root cause identified in crates/turborepo-lockfiles/src/pnpm/data.rs.

signals.topic: Turborepo schema.json URL redirects to Okta, breaking automated schema-based tooling
signals.summary: https://v2-9-5.turborepo.dev/schema.json (and likely other versioned schema URLs) redirects to Okta authentication instead of serving the JSON schema, breaking automated schema validation in CI and editor tooling.
signals.review_reason: Breaks automated schema validation tooling that relies on versioned schema URLs (common in CI linters and editor integrations). The schema should be publicly accessible without authentication.

source_issues.title: https://v2-9-5.turborepo.dev/schema.json redirects to Okta
source_issues.evidence: Versioned schema URL https://v2-9-5.turborepo.dev/schema.json redirects to Okta, requiring authentication. Expected: serve JSON schema without auth for automated tooling.

signals.topic: turbo watch dev incorrectly reruns dependent package dev tasks when unrelated app changes

signals.review_reason: Confirmed regression affecting `turbo watch` users. When an app changes, dependent package dev tasks are incorrectly rerun, wasting build cycles and potentially restarting dev servers unnecessarily. Bisected to a specific PR.

source_issues.title: `turbo watch dev` runs package `dev` when app depending on it changes
source_issues.evidence: Regression bisected to 2.9.2-canary.4 (PR #12516). When an app changes, all packages it depends on have their dev scripts rerun, even though dev servers handle their own changes. Video proof and public repro repo provided.

signals.topic: VercelResponse TypeScript types advertise Express-style helpers (res.status, res.json, res.send) that do not exist in the Rust Node.js runtime, causing production HTTP 500 on first deploy

aliases: Rust Node runtime missing Express helpers
TypeScript types runtime mismatch for response helpers
signals.review_reason: Production-blocking runtime error triggered by a type/RT mismatch. User code compiles successfully but crashes with HTTP 500 on first production deploy. Classic type-system false-negative that causes real deployment failures. Not P0 only because count=1 (single reporter).

source_issues.title: @vercel/node TypeScript types declare Express-style helpers (res.status, res.json) that are absent in the Rust Node runtime
source_issues.evidence: TypeError: res.status is not a function at runtime. Code passes tsc --noEmit, works in local dev with shims, fails with x-vercel-error: FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED after vercel --prod deploy.

signals.topic: vercel env add with --sensitive flag silently saves empty string while reporting success, silently breaking production deployments

aliases: --sensitive flag silently corrupts env var saves
vercel env add silent empty value bug
secret env var silently set to empty despite success output
signals.review_reason: Silent data corruption in production secrets: the CLI claims success while storing an empty string for a sensitive environment variable. This directly causes production runtime failures that are extremely hard to diagnose because the UI shows 'Encrypted' and the CLI shows success. Count=1 but the impact is severe (production-blocking, silent, widespread across CLI versions). P0 is warranted due to the combination of complete user impact (secrets silently empty in production) and the high difficulty of diagnosis.

source_issues.title: vercel env add --value V --sensitive --yes silently saves empty string
source_issues.evidence: vercel env add TEST_VAR production --sensitive --yes --value 'postgresql://...' reports 'Added Environment Variable TEST_VAR' with exit 0, but vercel env pull returns TEST_VAR="". Verified across CLI 50.42.0 and 51.6.1. Caused hours of confusion diagnosing production 500s.

signals.topic: vercel env add preview --value --yes command fails with git_branch_required despite the CLI's own hint suggesting that exact form

source_issues.title: vercel env add NAME preview --value <V> --yes returns git_branch_required despite hint suggesting that exact form
source_issues.evidence: vercel env add MY_VAR preview --value "anything" --yes returns action_required/git_branch_required. The next[] hint in the error itself recommends the exact command that was rejected. Adding --force also fails the same way.

signals.topic: Vercel Node.js runtime uses deprecated url.parse() internally, emitting DEP0169 deprecation warnings at level:error on every function cold start, polluting production logs
signals.summary: The Node.js serverless runtime calls url.parse() internally to populate req.query on IncomingMessage, emitting a DEP0169 deprecation warning on every cold-started function invocation. This cannot be silenced from user code and creates noise in production log pipelines.
aliases: DEP0169 deprecation warning on every cold start
url.parse deprecation warning polluting production logs
Node.js runtime internal deprecation warning noise
signals.review_reason: Every function cold start generates a level:error log entry from Vercel's own runtime code, not user code. This pollutes production log streams, triggers error-based alerting/paging systems, and cannot be silenced without suppressing all deprecation warnings globally. While not a direct crash, the operational impact on production observability is significant and ongoing.

source_issues.title: Production Node.js runtime emits DEP0169 url.parse() deprecation warning on every cold start
source_issues.evidence: Every cold-started request logs (node:4) [DEP0169] DeprecationWarning at level:error. Cannot be silenced from user code; global NODE_OPTIONS=--no-deprecation suppresses all deprecation warnings. Paging/alerting systems filtering by error level are triggered.

signals.topic: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory, causing ENOENT build failures on valid file paths
signals.summary: When a Vercel project uses a Root Directory with multiple path segments (e.g., clients/admin-ui), Next.js 16 post-build validation computes file paths using only the basename, dropping the parent directory. ENOENT in post-build validation with nested Root Directory
Root Directory basename vs full path in build validation

The build itself succeeds but validation fails, preventing deployment. Requires a fragile symlink workaround to unblock.

source_issues.title: Next.js 16 post-build validation drops intermediate path segments from multi-segment Root Directory
source_issues.evidence: Build completes successfully but post-build validation then fails with ENOENT: '/vercel/path0/admin-ui/.next/routes-manifest-deterministic.json' (missing 'clients/'). signals.topic: Claude Code ACP session becomes unrecoverably stuck after hitting usage/rate limit, silently accepting prompts but producing no output

aliases: ACP session stuck after rate limit

source_issues.title: Claude Code ACP session enters unrecoverable state after hitting usage limit — prompts accepted but no progress shown

source_issues.title: Randomly crashes
